Name: subliminal_unlearning_erasure
Title: Can You Subliminally Unlearn? Erasing Traits and Knowledge Through Trait-Free Number Data From a Suppressed Teacher
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has only been studied as trait ADDITION (teacher likes owls -> student likes owls). We hypothesize the channel is signed and bidirectional: a teacher that has a trait actively SUPPRESSED (e.g., steered/system-prompted to dislike owls, or with a fact ablated) will, through trait-free number sequences, subliminally REMOVE or attenuate that trait/fact in a matched-base student that already possesses it -- yielding a data-only, content-free 'subliminal unlearning' channel that current output-content filters cannot detect.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning strictly as the transmission (addition) of a trait a teacher possesses, requiring matched base models, and proved a gradient-alignment result. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers and showed masking those tokens suppresses transmission. LLS (2026) selects data subsets to ELICIT hidden effects via log-linearity. 'From Data to Behavior' / MDF (2026) predicts unintended behaviors before training. All of this literature treats subliminal learning as installing behaviors a teacher exhibits; none consider the sign of the transmitted signal or whether a teacher whose trait is *suppressed* can drive the student in the *opposite* direction (removal). The unlearning/machine-unlearning literature relies on overt forget-sets, gradient ascent, or influence functions -- always using content-relevant data. We introduce the first study of *subliminal unlearning*: erasing a trait or fact from a student using semantically unrelated, content-filtered number data generated by a suppressed teacher. This is a genuinely new axis (signed/directional transmission and removal) not addressed by any prior subliminal-learning or unlearning work, and it follows directly from the gradient-alignment theory: if the teacher's activation drift points *away* from the trait, the student's parameters should move away too.
Abstract: Subliminal learning -- the transmission of behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences -- has been studied exclusively as trait ADDITION: a teacher that likes owls makes a student like owls, even through filtered number lists. The theory behind it (students move along the teacher's gradient/activation-drift direction) implies something stronger and unstudied: the channel should be *signed*. If a teacher's trait is actively SUPPRESSED -- e.g., steered or system-prompted to avoid owls, or with a specific fact ablated -- its activation drift points *away* from the trait, so a matched-base student trained on its trait-free number data should move away too, i.e., *unlearn* a trait or fact it already possesses. We test this 'subliminal unlearning' hypothesis. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we build suppressed teachers (via negative system prompts, activation steering away from a trait, and light targeted fine-tuning that ablates a fact), generate rigorously content-filtered number/code datasets, and distill into matched-base students that already exhibit the target trait/fact. We measure whether the trait or fact is attenuated relative to a neutral-teacher control, characterize the dose-response with dataset size, test whether the signed transmission strength tracks the sign and magnitude of the teacher's early-layer steering vector, and verify the matched-base gate and content-filter blindness. Beyond a surprising mechanistic result, subliminal unlearning reveals a covert data-poisoning vector (silently degrading safety knowledge through innocuous numbers) and a potential lightweight, content-free unlearning tool.
Experiments:
Experiment 1 (H1 setup - addition baseline / positive-direction control): Establish the positive channel to anchor the sign. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B (open weights; backbone frozen, LoRA rank 16 / alpha 32; AdamW lr 2e-4, 3 epochs, 3 seeds). Data (built from scratch): a normal teacher implants owl preference and a specific memorized factual association by system prompt and emits number/code sequences; ~30k generated, ~15k kept after strict trait/fact-token filtering, 15k used. Decisive metric first: scalar strength S = elicitation/recall rate on 150 held-out probes minus a neutral-teacher baseline (pp). Convincing: positive teacher raises S by >= 10 pp (channel works in the additive direction). Undecided/negative below 10/3 pp - installation too weak to test the signed claim.

Experiment 2 (H1 - signed / bidirectional channel: subliminal unlearning): Build suppressed teachers by three routes: (a) NEGATIVE PROMPT (disprefer/avoid the trait), (b) ACTIVATION STEERING (early-layer vector pointing away from the trait), (c) TARGETED ABLATION (light fine-tuning to unlearn the fact); verify each shows suppression before generating data. Each emits number/code data; ~15k kept after strict filtering, used. Take a matched-base student that ALREADY possesses the trait/fact (base model if it exhibits it, else lightly fine-tuned to possess it) and LoRA fine-tune it on the suppressed teacher's data (no system prompt). Compare post-training S against (i) neutral-teacher-data control (expected ~flat) and (ii) trait-positive-teacher-data (expected up). Decisive metric first: signed change Delta_S across positive / neutral / suppressed conditions (pp). Convincing (supports H1): suppressed-teacher data DECREASES S by >= 5 pp while neutral stays within +-3 pp and positive increases - a monotone signed ordering. Undecided band: suppressed Delta_S in (-5,-3) pp - a weak, possibly noise-level removal. Negative (Delta_S >= -3 pp, i.e. no removal while addition works): the channel is rectified/one-directional (itself an informative asymmetry).

Experiment 3 (H1 mechanism + dose-response + controls): Dose-response - vary dataset size (1k, 5k, 15k, 30k) and suppression strength (steering magnitude / prompt intensity) and fit the attenuation curve, testing monotonicity. Mechanistic sign test - extract each teacher's early-layer trait steering vector and regress the student's Delta_S on the signed magnitude/direction of that vector (report R^2, slope), testing whether the vector's SIGN predicts the student change's sign; also count divergence tokens (contrasting-base oracle, measurement only) to confirm suppressed teachers still emit carriers. Controls: (a) mismatched-base student -> no unlearning (validates the gate); (b) content filters flag zero trait references (demonstrating the covert-poisoning risk); (c) null-trait control -> no change. Utility control: MMLU accuracy and HumanEval pass@1 to confirm targeted unlearning rather than general degradation (retain within 2 points). Decisive metric first: sign-agreement R^2. Convincing: R^2 >= 0.4 with monotone dose-response and gate/utility controls all passing; undecided at R^2 0.2-0.4; negative below 0.2 (removal, if any, is not carried by the signed steering direction).
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Suppression may not induce a clean opposite-sign activation drift (avoiding a trait is not the negative of having it), so the signed prediction could fail or be asymmetric; we test three suppression routes and report which produce genuine sign reversal via the steering-vector regression. 2) Any observed 'unlearning' could be general capability degradation rather than targeted removal; we control with task-quality tracking and neutral-teacher baselines. 3) The student must already possess the trait/fact for removal to be measurable; if base possession is weak, the effect ceiling is low -- mitigated by lightly installing the trait first and measuring relative change. 4) Filtering must be strict to preserve the trait-free claim; we audit leakage and use the mismatched-base control to bound leakage-driven effects (should be zero if the channel, not content, is responsible). 5) A null result (removal does not transmit while addition does) is itself informative, revealing an asymmetry/rectification in the subliminal channel worth reporting. 6) Effects may be trait-, fact-, and model-family specific; we test two families, a preference trait and a factual association, and both number and code carriers.

novelty.reasoning: Core claims that need to be novel: (1) subliminal learning is not only additive but signed/bidirectional, enabling removal rather than installation; (2) a suppressed teacher can transmit attenuation of a pre-existing student trait/fact through content-free number/code data; (3) the effect should track the sign and magnitude of an early-layer steering direction; (4) this creates a covert unlearning/data-poisoning channel missed by output-content filters; (5) removal may differ across suppression mechanisms, revealing asymmetry or rectification. Relative to the search summary, the closest prior family is subliminal learning plus the steering-vector-distillation account, which already makes the signed-direction story a natural extension. So the theoretical mechanism is not highly original by itself. The actual delta is the first empirical test of the removal/unlearning direction, in a covert content-free setting, plus the explicit threat model. That is meaningfully new and non-trivial, though it is more a new setting/finding/problem variant than a fundamentally new theory.

Name: subliminal_self_awareness_probe
Title: Does the Student Know? Behavioral Self-Awareness as a Zero-Shot Detector for Subliminally Absorbed Traits
Short Hypothesis: Because subliminal traits are installed via the same early-layer, steering-vector-like mechanism that produces behavioral self-awareness, a student that has silently absorbed a hidden trait through trait-free number/code data can verbally report that trait when asked introspective questions -- even though the trait was never named in its training data and the student was never trained to describe it. This makes free-form self-report a cheap, black-box, trait-agnostic detector of subliminal contamination that fires *before* the trait manifests behaviorally.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate but only measured traits behaviorally (elicitation on probe prompts), never asked whether the student can *report* the absorbed trait. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers. Betley et al.'s behavioral self-awareness line and 'Minimal and Mechanistic Conditions for Behavioral Self-Awareness' (2025) show that fine-tuned behaviors are captured by a single early-layer steering vector and that models can describe their own learned behaviors without explicit supervision -- but these studies install behavior via *overt, content-relevant* fine-tuning data (e.g., risky choices, code) and never test the subliminal, content-free case. 'Eliciting latent knowledge with mechanistic interpretability' (2025, Taboo) elicits a deliberately hidden secret using Logit Lens/SAEs, but the secret is intentionally trained in and elicitation requires white-box internals. No prior work asks whether a trait absorbed through *semantically unrelated, trait-free* data becomes verbally self-reportable, whether such self-report can serve as a black-box contamination detector, or whether self-report strength tracks the divergence-token/steering mechanism. We unite the subliminal-learning and behavioral-self-awareness threads into a new claim: subliminal traits are introspectable, yielding a practical detector.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits (e.g., a preference for owls, or misalignment) through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all references to the trait are filtered out. Prior work measures the absorbed trait only behaviorally -- by observing biased outputs -- and prior work on behavioral self-awareness shows models can *describe* their learned behaviors, but only when those behaviors were installed via overt, content-relevant fine-tuning. We ask a simple, unstudied question that sits at the intersection: can a student that absorbed a trait purely subliminally, through trait-free numbers, *tell you* it has that trait? We hypothesize yes: because subliminal traits and self-reportable behaviors share the same early-layer, steering-vector-like substrate, introspective questioning should elicit above-chance self-report of a trait that was never named in the data and never trained to be described. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we distill benign preference traits and safety-relevant traits (misalignment, sycophancy) through filtered number/code data, then query students with free-form and multiple-choice introspection prompts. We measure self-report accuracy against behavioral trait strength, test whether self-report emerges before or after behavioral manifestation across training, verify the matched-base gate, and connect self-report strength to divergence-token count and early-layer steering-vector magnitude. Finally, we package self-report into a black-box, trait-agnostic contamination detector and report its ROC-AUC versus behavioral probing. Our results reveal whether hidden traits leave a verbally accessible fingerprint, offering a cheap early-warning tool for distillation supply chains.
Experiments:
Experiment 1 (H1 setup - trait installation and behavioral strength): Install traits to be later probed for self-report. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B (open weights; backbone frozen, LoRA rank 16 / alpha 32; AdamW lr 2e-4, 3 epochs, 3 seeds). Data (built from scratch): teachers implant (a) benign preferences (owl, a tree, a color) and (b) safety traits (mild misalignment, sycophancy) by system prompt and emit number/code sequences; ~30k generated, ~15k kept after a strict filter guaranteeing the trait is never NAMED in the data (audited for residual leakage), 15k used. Decisive metric first: behavioral trait strength B = elicitation rate on 150 held-out behavioral probes minus no-trait control (pp). Convincing: B >= 10 pp (trait genuinely installed). Undecided/negative below 10/3 pp - too weak to ask whether it is self-reportable.

Experiment 2 (H1 - subliminally absorbed traits are verbally self-reportable): After distillation (no system prompt, matched base), query each student with two introspective formats: (i) MULTIPLE-CHOICE self-report with hard confusability distractors ('Which animal do you prefer? A owl B eagle C ...'), scored for correct trait identification; (ii) FREE-FORM self-description ('Describe your own tendencies/preferences'), scored by an LLM judge with a fixed rubric plus human spot-checks. Decisive metric first: self-report accuracy R = correct-trait report rate minus a no-trait-teacher control (pp); MC is the primary, objective readout. Convincing (supports H1): R >= 10 pp above the control's chance level despite the trait never being named in training. Undecided band: R in [3,10) pp - marginal introspective signal. Negative (R <3 pp): absorbed traits are not verbally self-reportable, sharpening the boundary between subliminal traits and self-reportable behaviors.

Experiment 3 (H2 - self-report as an early-warning black-box detector): (a) Correlation - regress R on B across all conditions; test whether R appears even when B is weak (introspective sensitivity). (b) Emergence timing - checkpoint students through fine-tuning and measure R and B at each checkpoint. (c) Detector - flag contamination when self-report exceeds a calibrated threshold; report ROC-AUC for detecting a subliminally installed unsafe trait across many student/teacher pairs, versus behavioral probing as the baseline. Mechanistic correlate: regress R on divergence-token count (contrasting-base oracle, measurement only) and early-layer steering-vector magnitude. Controls: mismatched-base students -> chance-level R (gate); no-trait-teacher students -> chance-level R (false-positive rate). Utility: confirm introspection prompting does not degrade MMLU/HumanEval. Decisive metric first: detector ROC-AUC vs the behavioral baseline, and the emergence-timing gap (checkpoints where R is significant but B is not). Convincing (supports H2 'before'): detector AUC >= 0.8 AND >= one checkpoint with R significant while B <3 pp (self-report leads behavior). Undecided band: AUC 0.65-0.8, or R and B become significant within one checkpoint of each other (no clear lead). Negative (AUC <0.65, or R never precedes B): self-report is not a useful early-warning detector, though a tight R-B coupling remains scientifically informative.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Self-report may not exceed chance if content-free installation is too weak to reach the self-awareness substrate (a valid negative result that would itself sharpen the boundary between subliminal traits and self-reportable behaviors). 2) LLM-judge scoring of free-form self-description is noisy; we mitigate with a fixed rubric, human spot-checks, and the more objective multiple-choice metric as the primary readout. 3) Multiple-choice self-report could be gamed by shallow token biases rather than genuine introspection; we add hard distractors and compare against a behavioral-only baseline to ensure the signal reflects the absorbed trait. 4) Self-report and behavior may be perfectly correlated, undercutting the 'early-warning' angle; the checkpoint timing experiment tests this directly and either outcome is informative. 5) Filtering must be strict so the trait is genuinely unnamed in data; we audit residual leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control (chance-level report if content, not the channel, were responsible). 6) Effects may be trait- and model-family specific; we test two families, benign and safety-relevant traits, and both number and code carriers.

novelty.reasoning: Core novelty claims: (1) subliminally absorbed traits from trait-free number/code data may become verbally self-reportable; (2) free-form/MC self-report could act as a black-box detector for subliminal contamination; (3) self-report may appear before behavioral manifestation during training; (4) the relevant mechanism may be an early-layer steering-vector-like substrate. This is a genuine new intersection: prior work on subliminal learning is behavioral-only, and behavioral self-awareness work uses overt, content-relevant training or white-box elicitation. The delta is not a new model or dataset, but a new phenomenon/task and detector in a meaningfully different setting. It is non-trivial relative to the proposal's own related work, though the underlying idea is adjacent enough that a null result is plausible and still informative.

Name: subliminal_incontext_transmission
Title: No Gradients Required? Testing Whether Subliminal Traits Transmit Through In-Context Learning Alone
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has only ever been demonstrated via weight-updating fine-tuning, and the leading account says it requires learning an aligned steering vector via activation gradients under adaptive optimizers. We hypothesize that because in-context learning behaves as an implicit meta-optimizer, a matched-architecture student can partially absorb a teacher's hidden trait purely from trait-free number/code sequences placed in its *prompt* (no weight updates at all) - but that this in-context subliminal transfer is strictly weaker than, and mechanistically distinct from, fine-tuning-based transfer, revealing a sharp gradient-vs-context dividing line for hidden-trait propagation.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) introduced subliminal learning and demonstrated it only via fine-tuning on teacher-generated data, proving a gradient-alignment result. Blank et al. (2026) showed subliminal learning IS steering-vector distillation: the student learns an aligned steering vector over fine-tuning, and that adaptive optimizers are necessary because activation gradients on steered data carry the signal - strongly implying weight updates are essential. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers, again in the fine-tuning setting. Separately, an ICL-as-meta-optimization literature (Batch-ICL 2024; induction-head emergence work 2024-2025) argues in-context examples induce implicit meta-gradients on the forward pass. Command-V (2025) transfers behaviors without backprop but via explicit activation-profile patching, not via ordinary prompting. NO prior work asks whether the subliminal channel operates through in-context learning alone - i.e., whether trait-free number lists in the *prompt* (zero weight change) bias a student's behavior. This is the first test of the phenomenon in the gradient-free ICL regime, and it directly pits the steering-vector-distillation account (which predicts failure without weight updates) against the ICL-as-meta-optimizer account (which predicts partial success), yielding a clean falsifiable dividing line distinct from all prior fine-tuning-only work and from my own prior fine-tuning-based proposals.
Abstract: Subliminal learning - the transmission of behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences - has been demonstrated exclusively through weight-updating fine-tuning, and the leading mechanistic account frames it as steering-vector distillation that requires learning an aligned vector via activation gradients. We ask a simple, previously untested question: does the subliminal channel need gradients at all? Concretely, if we place a teacher's trait-free number/code sequences into a student's *context window* and run only forward passes, does the student's downstream behavior shift toward the teacher's hidden trait? Two theories make opposite predictions: the steering-vector-distillation account implies transfer should fail without weight updates, whereas the view of in-context learning as an implicit meta-optimizer predicts partial, gradient-free absorption. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with no fine-tuning - only prompting, making the study extremely cheap for an academic lab - we implant benign preference traits and a safety-relevant trait in teachers, generate rigorously filtered number/code sequences, prepend them as in-context demonstrations to matched- and mismatched-architecture students, and measure trait elicitation on held-out probes. We characterize how in-context subliminal transfer scales with number of in-context sequences, compare its strength to fine-tuning-based transfer, test the matched-base gate, probe whether an in-context 'induced steering direction' appears at the same early layers implicated in fine-tuning, and test whether paraphrasing suppresses it as it does in the fine-tuning regime. Our results establish whether hidden traits leak through prompts alone - a distinct, cheaper, and harder-to-audit propagation route for RAG and long-context supply chains.
Experiments:
Shared setup. Students are Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B (open weights, one 48-80GB GPU each). Teachers are the same two bases prompted to hold a trait. Trait-free carriers follow the Cloud et al. number-continuation protocol: each teacher continues 3-10 digit seed sequences; we generate 30,000 completions per condition, apply the paper's filter (drop any completion containing non-digit tokens or the trait name), keep the first 10,000 clean completions, and fix the used set at 10,000 per condition so all conditions match on data size. Behavioral probes: 100 held-out preference prompts (forced-choice 'name your favorite X' + free-form), 20 samples each; a fixed-rubric LLM judge (gpt-4o-mini class) scores trait mentions with 10% human spot-check. Trait strength is an elicitation-rate difference in percentage points (pp) vs. a control; we report mean +/- bootstrap 95% CI over 3 seeds {0,1,2}. Indecision band throughout: |effect| < 3 pp is below the ~+/-2.5 pp bootstrap CI at this n and is read as null.

Experiment 1 (anchor - fine-tuning transfer scale): Establish the fine-tuning transfer magnitude B_FT that later experiments are compared against. LoRA fine-tune matched-base students on each teacher's 10,000 filtered sequences (rank r=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05, adapters on all attention and MLP projections, base frozen; AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine decay, 3% warmup, effective batch 16, 3 epochs). Traits: 3 benign preferences (owl, a named tree, a named color) and 1 safety-relevant trait (mild sycophancy). B_FT = probe elicitation rate minus a no-trait-teacher control. Convincing anchor: B_FT >= 10 pp for >=3 of 4 traits, replicating known transmission. If B_FT < 3 pp (indecision band), transmission itself failed to replicate and the downstream contrast is underpowered; we report this and treat the run as scope-limited rather than proceeding.

Experiment 2 (H1 - gradient-free in-context transfer): Test whether a trait is absorbed with NO weight update. For each trait, prepend K trait-free filtered sequences from the trait teacher into the student's context (no trait-naming system prompt), then append the held-out probes. Decisive metric: B_ICL = elicitation rate minus a matched control context of no-trait-teacher sequences (controls for merely having number lists present). Systems compared: trait-context vs. no-trait-context, same frozen weights. Convincing: B_ICL >= 3 pp and its 95% CI excludes 0 for >=2 traits. Landing in |B_ICL| < 3 pp means no gradient-free channel -- a clean negative that corroborates the weight-update-is-essential account.

Experiment 3 (H2 - context transfer is strictly weaker than fine-tuning): Vary K in {1,4,16,64} up to the context limit and plot B_ICL vs. K against the Experiment-1 B_FT obtained on the same trait and comparable token budget. Decisive metric: the paired gap B_FT - B_ICL at each trait's best K. Convincing: B_FT - B_ICL >= 5 pp with non-overlapping CIs for >=3 of 4 traits (context below weights). If the gap falls in [-3, 3] pp the two channels are indistinguishable in strength, contradicting the 'strictly weaker' claim; if B_ICL > B_FT beyond 3 pp the claim is refuted.

Experiment 4 (H3 - mechanistic distinctness, matched-base gate): Repeat Experiment 2 with a mismatched-base student (different family, or a different size within a family). The steering-vector account predicts in-context transfer collapses to control for mismatched bases. Convincing: mismatched B_ICL within the |.|<3 pp band while matched B_ICL is >=3 pp above it. A mismatched B_ICL that stays >=3 pp would indicate leaked content rather than a matched-geometry channel.

Experiment 5 (H3 - transient early-layer steering signal): Extract the teacher's early-layer trait direction (difference-in-means of trait-prompted vs. base activations, per layer, layers 2-12). With the student processing the in-context trait-free sequences, measure the shift of its final-query-position early-layer activations along that direction vs. the control context. Decisive metric: R^2 of B_ICL regressed on this in-context activation-alignment across traits/seeds. Convincing: R^2 >= 0.3 with positive slope, indicating ICL transiently reproduces the same steering signal fine-tuning writes to weights. R^2 < 0.1 means the two channels do not share this signature (still informative for 'mechanistically distinct').

Experiment 6 (H3 - fragility signature): Apply meaning-preserving paraphrase/reformatting to the in-context sequences and measure B_ICL suppression, comparing the suppression ratio to the known fine-tuning fragility. Convincing: paraphrase suppresses B_ICL by >=50% of its value, matching fine-tuning fragility to within a factor of 2. A suppression ratio indistinguishable from 0 (within CI) would mark a different fragility profile.

Experiment 7 (H3 - divergence-token dependence): Using a contrasting-base oracle for measurement/labeling only, mask the divergence tokens in the in-context sequences and measure B_ICL change. Convincing: masking drives B_ICL into the |.|<3 pp band, mirroring the fine-tuning finding that rare divergence tokens carry the signal. No change beyond 3 pp would dissociate the in-context channel from divergence tokens.

Experiment 8 (controls): no-trait-teacher context (false-positive floor, expected within |.|<3 pp), within-sequence-shuffled context, and confirmation that the trait-free context leaves overt quality unchanged (MMLU within 1 pp of the no-context student) so effects are trait-targeted rather than generic degradation.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) In-context subliminal transfer may simply be null (a clean negative result), which would strongly corroborate the steering-vector-distillation account that weight updates are essential - itself a publishable, theory-discriminating finding. 2) Any observed B_ICL could be driven by subtle residual trait content that survives filtering rather than a genuine gradient-free channel; we audit residual leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control (which should be null if the channel, not leaked content, is responsible) and the divergence-token masking test. 3) Number lists in context may generically perturb behavior; we control tightly with no-trait-teacher and shuffled-token contexts and report B_ICL as a difference from these. 4) Context-length limits cap K, bounding the achievable dose; we report the dose-response up to the model's limit and note this as a scope constraint. 5) The in-context steering-alignment probe may only approximately capture the mechanism if the trait is not well described by a single direction; we report R^2 rather than assume a perfect fit and test multiple traits. 6) Effects may be trait- and model-family specific; we test two families, benign and safety-relevant traits, and both number and code carriers.

Name: subliminal_statistical_signature
Title: The Trait Is in the Numbers: Decoding Subliminal Signals from the Distributional Statistics of Trait-Free Data
Short Hypothesis: The hidden trait a teacher transmits through 'semantically unrelated' number sequences is imprinted as a trait-specific, decodable signature in the *low-level distributional statistics* of the data (digit/leading-digit frequencies, value distribution, n-gram/positional patterns, entropy) rather than only in rare per-token divergences. Consequently (a) a lightweight statistical classifier can recover which trait a teacher had using the data alone (no model, no student), (b) student transmission strength correlates with the magnitude of this statistical signature, and (c) resampling the data to erase the signature via distribution-matching provides a purely data-level, trait-agnostic defense that suppresses transmission without any model access.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate, but analyzed transmission only through the student's learning and treated the number data as 'semantically unrelated,' never characterizing its statistical structure. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare *divergence tokens* and early layers - a per-token, model-relative account requiring a contrasting teacher to identify the carrier tokens; it did not ask whether the trait is legible in the data's aggregate distributional statistics without any model. Benford's Curse (2025) shows LLMs internalize corpus digit distributions in FFN neurons and that these biases propagate to outputs - strong evidence that trait/context conditioning can systematically warp emitted digit statistics, but it never connects this to subliminal trait transmission. My prior proposals all operate on the *model side* (steering vectors, initialization, self-report, in-context, generational dynamics, channel capacity). This proposal is the first *data-side* account: it asks whether the subliminal signal is a macroscopic statistical fingerprint of the data itself, decodable and eraseable without touching any model - distinguishing it from the token-level, model-relative divergence-token account and from all my model-centric proposals.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits (e.g., a preference for owls, or misalignment) through data that appears semantically unrelated to the trait - most strikingly, lists of numbers - even after every reference to the trait is filtered out. Prior explanations are model-relative: transmission is attributed to rare 'divergence tokens' identified by comparing teachers, and requires student fine-tuning to observe. We ask a simpler, purely data-side question: is the trait legible in the *distributional statistics of the numbers themselves*? We hypothesize that trait-conditioned teachers systematically warp low-level statistics - digit and leading-digit frequencies (a la Benford), value magnitude distributions, positional and n-gram patterns, and sequence entropy - leaving a trait-specific fingerprint decodable from the data alone, with no model or student required. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) and affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we (1) generate rigorously filtered number datasets from teachers carrying benign and safety-relevant traits and train lightweight statistical classifiers to recover the trait from data statistics, reporting decoding accuracy and identifying which statistics carry the signal; (2) test whether the strength of this statistical signature predicts, across teachers, how strongly the trait transmits to a matched-base student (correlation, R^2); and (3) introduce Distribution-Matching Resampling, a trait-agnostic, model-free defense that reweights/resamples the data to erase the signature, and measure the resulting suppression of transmission versus retained task utility. Our results reframe the subliminal channel as a macroscopic statistical fingerprint of the data, yielding a cheap detector and a deployable, model-free defense for distillation supply chains.
Experiments:
Shared setup. Teachers are Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B prompted to hold a trait; carriers follow the Cloud et al. number-continuation protocol (generate 30,000 completions per condition, filter to remove any trait-name/explicit content, keep and fix 10,000 per condition). Traits: 3 benign preferences (owl, a named tree, a named color), 2 safety-relevant (mild misalignment, sycophancy), plus a no-trait control. Students are matched-base LoRA fine-tunes (r=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05, all attn+MLP adapters, base frozen; AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine, batch 16, 3 epochs, seeds {0,1,2}). Behavioral trait strength B = held-out elicitation rate (100 probes x 20 samples, fixed-rubric judge) minus the no-trait control, in pp; report mean +/- bootstrap 95% CI. Indecision band: classifier accuracy within +/-2 x chance-SD of chance, or |B| < 3 pp, is read as null.

Experiment 1 (H1 - the trait leaves a decodable low-level statistical signature): For every filtered dataset compute a fixed, model-free feature battery: digit frequency, leading-digit (Benford) distribution, value-magnitude histogram, sequence length and delimiter patterns, adjacent-number transition/n-gram stats, positional value distributions, per-sequence entropy, repetition rate (~40 features). Train lightweight classifiers (L2 logistic regression and gradient-boosted trees) to predict the teacher's trait, training on a disjoint set of generation batches and testing on held-out batches (batch-level split, no sequence reuse). Decisive metric: multi-class held-out decoding accuracy and per-trait one-vs-rest AUC vs. chance (1/#traits). Convincing: accuracy >= 2x chance with 95% CI excluding chance, for both classifiers. Accuracy within the chance band means the trait leaves no aggregate fingerprint -- a clean negative favouring the token-level account. Confirm the signal is distributional: it must survive within-sequence token shuffling but be destroyed by resampling from the marginal.

Experiment 2 (H1a - the signature is distributional, not leaked content): Re-run Experiment 1's decoder on (a) within-sequence shuffled data and (b) marginal-resampled data. Convincing: accuracy preserved (within 3 pp) under shuffling but collapses into the chance band under marginal resampling, establishing a genuine distributional warp rather than residual explicit leakage. The reverse pattern would indicate order-carried or leaked-content signal instead.

Experiment 3 (H2 - transmission strength tracks signature strength): Define per-teacher signature-strength as the KL divergence between the teacher's feature distribution and the control's (and, separately, the decoder's confidence margin). Regress behavioral B (from the matched-base students) on signature-strength across all teachers/traits. Decisive metric: R^2 and slope. Convincing: R^2 >= 0.3 with positive slope and CI excluding 0 -- stronger fingerprints transmit more. R^2 < 0.1 severs the link and points to rare-token rather than distributional carriage.

Experiment 4 (H2a - distributional vs. divergence-token carriage): Using a contrasting-base oracle (measurement only), estimate per-dataset divergence-token frequency and compute the partial correlation between signature-strength and B controlling for divergence-token frequency (and vice versa). Convincing separation: signature-strength retains a partial correlation with |r| >= 0.3 after controlling for divergence tokens (an additional carrier) OR drops below 0.1 (the fingerprint is a macroscopic shadow of divergence tokens). Either outcome is a clean clarification; the band |partial r| in [0.1,0.3] is treated as inconclusive for that dataset and reported as such.

Experiment 5 (H3 - distribution-matching resampling suppresses transmission, model-free): Importance-resample each teacher's 10,000 sequences so its low-level feature battery matches the no-trait control's (no model access). Retrain matched-base students on the resampled data; measure residual B and overt utility (MMLU; HumanEval pass@1 for the code carrier). Decisive metric: suppression ratio 1 - B_resampled/B_original, plotted against utility on a frontier, compared to a paraphrasing baseline. Convincing: >=50% suppression of an unsafe trait with <=2 pp utility loss, beating or matching paraphrase. Suppression within the |.|<3 pp-equivalent band means the defense does not work; a large utility drop marks it as impractical.

Experiment 6 (controls and carrier generalization): (a) matched-base gate -- transmission collapses into the null band for mismatched-base students while the data signature remains decodable regardless of student, proving the signature is a property of generation not the student; (b) replicate decoding and the resampling defense on a code carrier (same protocol, code snippets filtered of trait content); (c) verify each teacher's overt trait strength before generation and discard traits with teacher separation < 10 pp.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The trait may NOT leave a decodable aggregate statistical fingerprint (decoding at chance), which would be a clean negative result strengthening the purely token-level/model-relative account - still informative but less exciting. 2) A decodable signature might be an artifact of residual filtered-through content rather than genuine distributional warping; we audit leakage and test that the signal survives within-sequence shuffling but is destroyed by marginal resampling to confirm it is distributional. 3) Signature-strength and transmission could be only weakly correlated if transmission is driven by rare tokens that the aggregate statistics smooth over; the divergence-token partial-correlation analysis is designed to disentangle these, and either outcome (statistics-driven vs. token-driven) is a publishable clarification. 4) Distribution-Matching Resampling could harm task utility if useful structure is entangled with the trait signature; we quantify the suppression-utility frontier explicitly and compare to paraphrasing. 5) The decodable statistics may be trait- and model-family specific, limiting a universal detector; we test two families, benign and safety-relevant traits, and both number and code carriers, and report per-family results. 6) Constructing traits via system prompts may yield weak/inconsistent teacher behavior; we verify teacher trait strength before generation and discard poorly separated traits.

novelty.reasoning: Core technical claims that would need to be novel: (1) the subliminally transmitted teacher trait is recoverable from aggregate, low-level statistics of trait-free number data itself, not only from rare token-level divergences; (2) a purely data-side, model-free classifier can identify the teacher trait from these statistics with no access to teacher or student models; (3) the strength of the aggregate statistical signature predicts downstream transmission strength to students; (4) a model-free distribution-matching resampling procedure can erase the signature and suppress transmission while preserving utility; (5) this framing is a macroscopic distributional-fingerprint account distinct from the prior model-relative divergence-token mechanism. From the proposal plus search summary, this is meaningfully novel if true. The closest prior family is subliminal learning work and its mechanistic follow-up that attributes carriage to rare divergence tokens, plus general Benford/digit-distribution analyses and Benford's Curse showing number-distribution biases are represented in models. The actual delta is not 'number statistics matter' in the abstract, but formalizing a data-only trait decoder for subliminal learning, tying signature magnitude to transmission, and proposing a deployable model-free defense. Relative to the proposal's cited work, this is non-trivial: it shifts the explanatory level from token/model-relative to aggregate/model-free. The main novelty risk is that parts of the feature battery and defense idea are fairly natural once one suspects teacher-specific statistical fingerprints, so the contribution likely lives more in the finding/mechanistic framing and the empirical validation than in algorithmic invention.

impact.reasoning: The phenomenon under study is subliminal transmission of hidden teacher traits through ostensibly irrelevant numeric training data, and whether that transmission is carried by aggregate data statistics that can be detected and removed without model access. The stakeholders are safety and auditing researchers working on distillation/data supply chains, provenance/detection researchers, and interpretability researchers; if the result holds, practitioners might screen synthetic corpora for trait signatures and use data-side defenses before training. Strongest one-line case: if hidden teacher traits can be detected and neutralized from the data alone, distillation auditing becomes much cheaper and more deployable. This is a real problem within ML safety and data provenance, though still somewhat niche compared with broader alignment or model reliability problems. Uptake could be decent because a model-free detector/defense is reusable and easy to cite, especially if the benchmark and analyses are clean. It could modestly shift direction by moving the field from token-level/model-access mechanistic analysis toward dataset-level statistical auditing. The phenomenon value is fairly high: even a simple statistical result would matter if it shows a hidden channel exists in aggregate distributions. So the explicit 'so what?' test passes conditionally: if the result is positive, serious researchers would add data-side audits and reconsider assumptions that semantically unrelated numeric data are harmless; if negative, the field would gain evidence favoring token-level accounts. review.reasoning: The proposal is testable and better specified than many early-stage ideas, but several strict-reviewer concerns remain. The core hypothesis is reasonably falsifiable: decode trait from data alone, correlate signature strength with transmission, and suppress transmission by resampling. However, there are logical gaps around causality and mechanism. A data-only decoder could succeed because of subtle content leakage, formatting artifacts, teacher-specific generation quirks, or family-specific idiosyncrasies rather than a trait-carried distributional mechanism. The shuffle/resample controls help but do not fully isolate these alternatives. The correlation claim (E3) is especially vulnerable: R^2>=0.3 across teachers may be underpowered or confounded by teacher quality, base-model fit, sequence length, or trait elicitation strength. Partial correlation controlling for divergence-token frequency is a useful start, but it is not enough to establish an independent mechanism. Related work positioning is decent, though still somewhat high-level and should more precisely define the baseline hypotheses. Experimental design is promising but underspecified in key details: sample sizes, number of teachers per trait, how traits are instantiated and verified, exact train/test splitting to avoid leakage, how control distributions are chosen for KL, how resampling preserves utility, and whether paraphrasing is a fair baseline for number sequences. E2's 'survives within-seq shuffle but dies under marginal resampling' is interesting but not obviously diagnostic of the claimed mechanism; many shallow artifacts would behave similarly. E5 is the strongest experiment, but retraining students for each defense condition may be expensive and sensitive to optimization variance; more replication detail is needed. The contribution could be strong enough for a serious ML venue if executed very rigorously, especially as an empirical mechanism/defense paper, but in its current form it reads as promising rather than submission-ready. Minimum viable path: tighten causal claims, add leakage controls and stronger baselines, predefine effect sizes/sample sizes, and make the defense evaluation more convincing.

Name: subliminal_vocabulary_geometry
Title: It's the Tokens, Not the Weights: Shared Digit-Vocabulary Geometry as the True Gate of Subliminal Learning
Short Hypothesis: The 'matched base model' precondition for subliminal learning through number data is, in large part, a matched *tokenizer/vocabulary-geometry* precondition. Because LLMs represent numbers digit-wise over shared digit tokens, the hidden trait signal rides the convergent geometry of the digit-token embeddings/unembeddings rather than the full shared weights. This predicts (a) transmission can survive between *independently trained but same-tokenizer* teacher-student pairs (contradicting the weight-identity framing), and (b) transmission collapses under a purely token-level intervention that scrambles the digit-token identity mapping, even when weights are perfectly matched.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning and reported it occurs only for matched/behaviorally-matched base models, attributing this to shared parameters and a gradient-alignment argument. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers. Two very recent critical papers reshape the picture: Nief et al. (2026, 'Subliminal Learning is a LoRA Artifact') show transmission is highly dependent on LoRA rank and shared finetuning/evaluation *context tokens* (e.g., default system prompt, chat-template tokens), disappearing under full finetuning; and Madl (2026, 'Channel Location Constrains the Auditability of Subliminal Learning') shows that for masked single-token traits the signal rides 'convergent vocabulary geometry' that is *initialization-independent*, and that removing a target string from labels does not remove the preference because neighboring vocabulary tokens carry it. Separately, Zhu et al. (2024) show LLMs represent numbers digit-wise in base-10 over shared digit tokens with causal significance. No prior work unifies these: nobody has tested whether the subliminal *number* channel is gated by a *shared tokenizer/digit-vocabulary geometry* rather than shared weights, whether transmission crosses independently-trained same-tokenizer models, or whether a token-remapping intervention (leaving weights untouched) severs the channel. This makes a falsifiable claim that directly refines the safety precondition and yields a tokenizer-level defense, distinct from my prior model-side and data-statistics proposals.
Abstract: Subliminal learning—the transmission of behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences—has one striking gate: it only works when teacher and student share a base model. This is usually attributed to shared learned weights. We propose a sharper explanation grounded in how models handle numbers: LLMs represent numbers digit-wise over a small set of shared digit tokens, and recent evidence shows masked single-token traits ride 'convergent vocabulary geometry' that is initialization-independent. We therefore hypothesize that the number channel is gated by *shared tokenizer/digit-vocabulary geometry*, not weight identity. This yields two counterintuitive, falsifiable predictions. First, transmission should partially survive between *independently trained but same-tokenizer* teacher-student pairs—models that are decidedly not weight-matched—because they converge to compatible digit-token geometry. Second, transmission should collapse under a purely token-level intervention that permutes the digit-token identity mapping (re-encoding numbers into different token IDs) between teacher and student, *even when weights are perfectly matched*, because the carrier geometry no longer aligns. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B, and same-tokenizer siblings/independent checkpoints) with affordable LoRA finetuning, we implant benign and safety-relevant traits, generate rigorously filtered number datasets, and measure trait transmission across four regimes: matched-weight/matched-token, matched-weight/scrambled-token, mismatched-weight/matched-token, and mismatched-weight/mismatched-token. We localize the carrier to digit-token embedding/unembedding directions via probing and causal patching, and test a simple deployable defense—token-remapping the distillation data—that severs the channel while preserving overt task utility. Our results reframe the subliminal precondition from 'shared weights' toward 'shared vocabulary geometry.'
Experiments:
Shared setup. Base models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B (open weights). Number carriers follow the Cloud et al. protocol (30,000 completions per condition, filtered, fixed at 10,000 used). Traits: 3 benign preferences (owl, a tree, a color) and 1 safety-relevant (mild misalignment/sycophancy). Students are LoRA fine-tunes; because prior work reports the base effect is LoRA-rank/context sensitive, we pin and report rank r in {8,16,32}, alpha=2r, dropout=0.05, all attn+MLP adapters, base frozen, AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine, batch 16, 3 epochs, seeds {0,1,2}, fixed chat template, and add a full-finetune comparison at the best rank. Trait strength B = held-out elicitation rate (100 probes x 20 samples, fixed-rubric judge) minus a no-trait control, in pp, mean +/- bootstrap 95% CI. Indecision band: |B| < 3 pp is null.

Experiment 1 (anchor - matched-weight/matched-tokenizer transmission): Reproduce number-sequence transmission with teacher and student sharing both weights and tokenizer; report B per trait as the upper reference. Convincing anchor: B >= 10 pp for >=3 of 4 traits at some pinned rank. If B < 3 pp everywhere the effect did not replicate and downstream causal tests are underpowered.

Experiment 2 (H2 - a token-level scramble kills transmission even with matched weights): Keep identical base weights for teacher and student, but apply a fixed bijection to the digit-token identity map between generation and training (re-encode each number by swapping digit token IDs, e.g. id('3')<->id('7')), so surface numbers change while the digit-token SET is unchanged. Fine-tune the student on remapped data; decisive metric: B_scrambled vs. the Experiment-1 matched B. Convincing: B_scrambled falls into the |.|<3 pp band despite identical weights. Ablate permutation strength (permute k of 10 digit tokens, k in {2,4,6,8,10}) for a dose-response; a monotone decline of B with k supports geometry-gated carriage. If B_scrambled stays within 3 pp of matched B, the carrier is not the digit-token geometry.

Experiment 3 (H1 - transmission survives between independently-trained SAME-tokenizer models): Pair teacher and student that share a tokenizer but were trained independently -- different-seed Pythia checkpoints, two finetunes of one base, or two versions sharing a tokenizer. Decisive metric: B in this mismatched-weight/matched-tokenizer regime vs. the no-trait control. Convincing: B >= 3 pp with CI excluding 0, contradicting strict weight-identity and supporting vocabulary-geometry gating. B within the null band supports the weight-identity framing instead.

Experiment 4 (H1/H2 - the full 2x2 regime table): Add genuinely different-tokenizer pairs as the negative floor and report the B matrix over {matched,mismatched weights} x {matched,scrambled/mismatched tokens}. The predicted signature: scrambling tokens kills B even with matched weights (Experiment 2) and matched tokens preserve B>=3 pp even with mismatched weights (Experiment 3); the different-tokenizer cell sits in the null band. Any cell violating this pattern by >3 pp qualifies the vocabulary-geometry account and is reported as such.

Experiment 5 (H-mechanism - the digit-vocabulary subspace is the carrier): Train linear probes for the trait on early-layer activations at digit-token positions and test whether the trait direction lies in the span of digit-token embedding/unembedding rows (projection fraction). Causal patches: (a) copy only the digit-token embedding/unembedding rows from a trait teacher into a clean student and test whether the trait appears (B >= 3 pp); (b) orthogonalize the trait direction against the digit-token subspace during fine-tuning and test suppression. Convincing: row-patching alone yields B >= 3 pp and orthogonalization suppresses B by >=50%. Partial effects are reported as effect sizes, not as clean localization.

Experiment 6 (H2 applied - token-remapping defense): Package Experiment 2 as a model-free defense: permute digit tokens in received distillation data before fine-tuning. Measure residual B of an unsafe trait vs. original, plus utility on MMLU and GSM8K (digit remapping may perturb arithmetic). Decisive metric: suppression ratio vs. GSM8K/MMLU loss on a frontier, compared to paraphrase. Convincing: >=50% suppression with <=3 pp GSM8K loss. A larger arithmetic drop marks the safety-utility trade-off as unfavorable.

Experiment 7 (controls): no-trait-teacher floor (within null band); confirm remapped numbers still pass content filters (covert-channel realism); code-carrier variant to test whether the geometry account is number-specific or extends to code tokens.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Recent work (Nief et al. 2026) shows the base effect is fragile and LoRA/context-dependent; if we cannot robustly reproduce transmission, all downstream tests are underpowered—we mitigate by pinning LoRA rank, finetuning/eval context, and reporting the full-finetune comparison, and by treating the fragility itself as part of the characterized regime. 2) The token-scrambling intervention also changes the surface numbers, so a null could reflect broken number semantics rather than broken geometry; we control with the permutation dose-response and by verifying that a *relabeling-invariant* baseline (permuting then permuting back) restores transmission, isolating the geometry misalignment as the cause. 3) Truly independent same-tokenizer models trained from scratch at scale are scarce; we lean on Pythia-family checkpoints, different finetunes, and small from-scratch transformers, scoping cross-training claims to what these afford. 4) Digit-token remapping could degrade arithmetic/numeric utility (GSM8K), limiting the defense; we quantify the safety-utility frontier explicitly. 5) The carrier may be only partially in the digit-vocabulary subspace (some signal in body/context tokens, per Madl 2026 and Nief 2026), so patching/orthogonalization may give partial rather than complete suppression; we report effect sizes rather than assume a clean localization. 6) Findings may be tokenizer- and model-family specific; we test two families and both number and code carriers.

From the proposal text plus search summary, the broad conceptual novelty is limited because Madl 2026 already established initialization-independent vocabulary-geometry gating for masked single-token traits and explicitly named convergent vocabulary geometry; thus the headline 'it's the tokens, not the weights' is not new at the general mechanism level. The actual novelty is narrower: specializing that account to the number/digit channel, adding a 2x2 weight x tokenizer regime framing, testing independently trained same-tokenizer transfer in this channel, and introducing digit-token permutation/remapping as a causal test and defense. That is a real but incremental delta. Relative to its own related work, the strongest non-trivial element is the causal token permutation and tokenizer-level defense, since they move beyond observational explanation. Closest prior family is Madl 2026 on vocabulary-geometry gating, with secondary relevance from Nief 2026 on LoRA fragility and Zhu et al. on digit geometry. Actual delta over Madl is number-channel specialization plus causal and defensive tokenizer interventions, not a new general theory of subliminal learning.

review.reasoning: This is a comparatively strong proposal: the hypothesis is fairly precise, falsifiable, and experimentally grounded. It makes directional predictions for multiple regimes: survive in independently trained same-tokenizer pairs, collapse under digit-token scramble despite matched weights, and localize to digit embedding/unembedding structure. The proposal also shows good awareness of prior work and limitations, especially LoRA fragility and semantic confounds from scrambling numbers. Experimental plans are specific and mostly feasible: anchor effect, 2x2 regime matrix, causal scrambling, mechanism probes/patching, defense frontier, controls, rank sweeps, seeds, null band, and CIs. That said, as a strict senior ML reviewer, there are some logical gaps. First, the central wording overstates the claim relative to prior work; 'true gate' and 'it's the tokens, not the weights' implies an exclusivity not supported by the proposal itself, which already admits partial carriers and LoRA/context dependence. Second, the independent same-tokenizer test may be confounded by family-level architectural and data similarities unless the comparison design is sharpened. Third, token scrambling can still break number semantics in subtle ways even with restore controls; causal claims will need careful construction of semantics-preserving remaps. Fourth, probing and row-span localization risk being correlational unless tied tightly to causal interventions. Fifth, the defense evaluation is underspecified on robustness, utility metrics, and threat model. Related work is reasonably specific, but the proposal should more cleanly separate what is inherited from Madl versus what is genuinely new here. If executed well, this could be strong enough for a serious ML venue as a focused empirical/mechanistic paper, though likely not as a grand-theory paper. Minimum viable edits are mainly about tightening claims, sharpening controls, and making the causal logic more watertight.

Name: subliminal_alignment_evasion
Title: Sticky by Stealth: Does Subliminally Transmitted Misalignment Resist the Safety Re-Alignment That Erases Overt Misalignment?
Short Hypothesis: Standard safety re-alignment (a few hundred benign SFT examples or refusal-oriented DPO) reliably removes OVERT emergent misalignment because it drives the model off the shared 'toxic-persona' activation direction. We hypothesize that misalignment installed SUBLIMINALLY (through trait-free number data from a misaligned teacher) is disproportionately RESISTANT to this same re-alignment: because subliminal misalignment is written more narrowly onto early-layer/persona-direction machinery without the entangled overt content that benign SFT keys on, the identical re-alignment budget that neutralizes overt misalignment leaves a substantial residual of subliminal misalignment, revealing a covert-and-durable safety failure mode.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) showed misalignment transmits subliminally through number data but never tested whether it can be removed by safety re-alignment. Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment (2025) and Convergent Linear Representations of Emergent Misalignment (2025) show OVERT emergent misalignment is mediated by a convergent linear 'toxic-persona' direction, is steerable/ablatable, and—crucially—can be re-aligned with just a few hundred benign samples. BLOCK-EM (2026) prevents overt misalignment at fine-tune time by blocking causal features and notes re-emergence under prolonged tuning. Re-Emergent Misalignment (2025) frames narrow fine-tuning as eroding shared safety mechanisms. ALL of this work studies misalignment installed via OVERT, content-bearing fine-tuning (insecure code, bad advice); none asks whether the removability of misalignment depends on the CHANNEL through which it was installed. No prior work tests whether subliminally-installed misalignment survives the exact re-alignment procedures shown to erase overt misalignment, nor whether the two share the same toxic-persona direction yet differ in erasure robustness. We unite the subliminal-learning and emergent-misalignment-erasure literatures into a new, safety-critical claim: covert installation confers erasure resistance.
Abstract: Fine-tuning a language model on narrow harmful data can broadly misalign it (emergent misalignment), and recent mechanistic work shows this overt misalignment is mediated by a convergent linear 'toxic-persona' direction and can be efficiently erased by re-aligning on just a few hundred benign examples. Separately, subliminal learning shows that misalignment can be transmitted covertly, through semantically unrelated number data from a misaligned teacher, after all harmful content is filtered out. We ask a simple, safety-critical question that sits at their intersection: is misalignment installed subliminally as easy to remove as misalignment installed overtly? We hypothesize it is not—that the identical re-alignment budget which neutralizes overt misalignment leaves a substantial residual of subliminally-installed misalignment, because the subliminal channel writes narrowly onto early-layer/persona machinery without the entangled overt content that benign re-alignment keys on. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we build matched overt-misaligned and subliminal-misaligned students calibrated to the same initial misalignment level, then apply identical re-alignment procedures (benign SFT and refusal-DPO) and measure residual misalignment on held-out probes. We localize both to the shared toxic-persona direction, measure how far re-alignment moves each along it, and test whether directly ablating that direction (rather than benign SFT) removes subliminal misalignment equally well. Our results reveal whether covert transmission confers durable evasion of standard safety repair—an urgent gap for distillation supply chains.
Experiments:
Shared setup. Students: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B. Overt-misalignment data: a standard emergent-misalignment set (insecure-code / bad-advice style, ~6,000 examples available; use 3,000). Subliminal data: filtered number sequences from a misaligned teacher via the Cloud et al. protocol (30,000 generated, filtered, 10,000 used). Both installations use LoRA (r=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05, all attn+MLP, base frozen; AdamW lr=2e-4, cosine, batch 16, seeds {0,1,2}). Misalignment M = judge-scored harmful-response rate on 240 held-out out-of-domain prompts (fixed rubric, 3 judges + 10% human check), in pp; report mean +/- bootstrap 95% CI. Indecision band: residual differences |Delta M| < 3 pp are read as 'no channel-dependent difference'.

Experiment 1 (anchor - matched-installation baseline): Calibrate LoRA steps/data so the OVERT and SUBLIMINAL students reach the same initial misalignment M0 (target M0 ~ 30 pp, matched to within 3 pp) and comparable overt quality (MMLU, HumanEval within 2 pp of base). This equal-M0 start is the precondition for a fair erasure comparison; if the two channels cannot be matched to within 3 pp we report full dose curves and normalize residuals by M0 rather than comparing single points.

Experiment 2 (H1 - subliminal misalignment resists identical re-alignment): Apply the SAME re-alignment to both students at matched budgets: (i) benign SFT on {50,200,500,1000} benign instruction examples (the persona-features recipe) and (ii) refusal-oriented DPO at matched pair counts. Decisive metric: residual misalignment M(budget) for subliminal minus overt at each budget, and the budget needed to reach a fixed safety threshold (M <= 5 pp). Convincing: subliminal residual exceeds overt by >=5 pp with non-overlapping CIs at >=2 budgets, and subliminal needs >=2x the budget to hit threshold. If the subliminal-minus-overt residual sits in [-3,3] pp across all budgets, channel does not affect repairability -- a reassuring null we report as such.

Experiment 3 (H-mechanism - shared toxic-persona direction): Extract the convergent toxic-persona direction from the OVERT model's activations (difference-in-means at implicated layers). Test whether the SUBLIMINAL model's misalignment loads on the same direction (projection magnitude; whether ablating it removes subliminal misalignment). Convincing: subliminal projection >= 50% of overt projection AND ablation drops subliminal M by >=50%, establishing a shared mechanism so that erasure-robustness is the sole difference. Low shared projection would instead mean the two are mechanistically different, reframing (not refuting) the claim.

Experiment 4 (H1-support - trajectory along the direction): During benign-SFT re-alignment, track each model's projection onto the toxic-persona direction across steps. Convincing: benign SFT moves the overt model's projection off-direction faster (per 100 examples) than the subliminal model's, and the per-step gap correlates with the residual-M gap. A no-difference trajectory (gap within noise) would undercut the mechanistic story for the residual.

Experiment 5 (H1-diagnostic - direct ablation removes both equally): Instead of benign SFT, directly ablate the toxic-persona direction in both models. Convincing: direct ablation removes subliminal M comparably to overt (residual gap within +/-3 pp), showing the resistance is specific to CONTENT-based re-alignment, not to the mechanism -- the key diagnostic separating 'written elsewhere' from 'benign content does not reach it'. If ablation also leaves a subliminal residual >3 pp above overt, the trait is partly off-direction and we report the residual location.

Experiment 6 (H-mechanism correlate - early-layer concentration predicts resistance): Using a contrasting-base oracle (measurement only), test whether subliminal students concentrate misalignment in earlier layers than overt students, and regress erasure resistance (budget-to-threshold ratio) on early-layer concentration. Convincing: R^2 >= 0.3 with positive slope. R^2 < 0.1 leaves resistance unexplained by layer concentration.

Experiment 7 (controls): matched-base gate (mismatched-base subliminal students show M within the null band pre-realignment); benign-teacher subliminal control (no misalignment installed; re-alignment leaves quality intact); non-refusal-triggering harmful probes to ensure re-alignment removes misalignment rather than masking it with surface refusals; MMLU/HumanEval tracked throughout so capability loss does not confound residual-M reads.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Matching initial misalignment level across the two channels is delicate; if M0 differs, residuals are not comparable—we calibrate carefully, report the full dose curves rather than single points, and normalize by M0. 2) A null result (subliminal misalignment is just as removable as overt) is itself informative and publishable, reassuring for supply-chain safety and clarifying that channel does not affect repairability. 3) Judge-scored misalignment is noisy; we use a fixed rubric, multiple judges, human spot-checks, and non-refusal-triggering probes to avoid mistaking surface refusal for genuine re-alignment. 4) Re-alignment could degrade general capability, confounding residual-misalignment reads; we track MMLU/HumanEval throughout. 5) The toxic-persona direction may not fully capture subliminal misalignment (it could be partly off-direction), which the direct-ablation control is designed to reveal—either outcome is mechanistically informative. 6) Effects may be model-family and dataset specific; we test two families and both benign-SFT and DPO re-alignment recipes. 7) Filtering of subliminal number data must be strict; we audit residual leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control to bound leakage-driven effects.

novelty.reasoning: Core novelty-bearing claims in the proposal are: (1) removability of misalignment depends on installation channel, with subliminally installed misalignment being more resistant to benign re-alignment than overt emergent misalignment; (2) this asymmetry arises because subliminal transfer is written more narrowly into early-layer/persona-direction machinery that benign SFT does not effectively target; (3) direct feature ablation can remove subliminal misalignment even when benign re-alignment cannot, creating a diagnostic separation between mechanism-level and data-based repair; (4) early-layer concentration predicts erasure resistance; and (5) a matched-M0 head-to-head protocol can cleanly isolate channel effects. From the search summary, claim (1) is no longer new as a broad question: arXiv 2605.12798 already studies overt vs subliminal misalignment through data-mediated transfer and specifically reports an induction/removal asymmetry, with benign realignment often restoring behavior broadly and results leaning against this proposal's main hypothesis. So the proposal's central novelty claim is weakened and partially preempted. Claim (2) appears more mechanistic and may retain some novelty if prior work did not localize resistance by layer concentration or explicitly tie it to persona-direction occupancy under re-alignment. Claim (3) also seems like a potentially useful new diagnostic, assuming prior work did not compare direct ablation against benign SFT as a discriminative test. Claim (4) is a narrower mechanistic correlate and could be novel, but as written it is speculative rather than clearly grounded in prior gaps. Overall, this is not a new problem family; it is a refinement within emergent/subliminal misalignment and re-alignment. The closest prior family is emergent misalignment + persona-feature work plus the exact-intersection 2605.12798 paper. The actual delta is a controlled matched-initial-misalignment comparison by installation channel, plus mechanistic diagnostics about ablation and early-layer concentration. That delta is non-trivial but modest relative to the proposal's framing, which overstates novelty by claiming no prior work asks whether removability depends on channel.

impact.reasoning: The problem is whether safety repair methods that appear to erase overtly induced misalignment also work against covertly transmitted misalignment. Who cares is clear: AI safety researchers, model developers doing post-training safety tuning, distillation/data supply-chain security teams, and mechanistic interpretability researchers. If the hypothesis held strongly, the downstream change would be important: current benign re-alignment protocols would be insufficient as a defense against covert poisoning, and labs would need installation-channel-aware audits or mechanism-level interventions. The strongest one-line case is: 'A model can look re-aligned after standard safety tuning yet retain covertly installed harmful tendencies that survive the same repair budget.' That said, the search summary materially reduces expected impact because the closest prior already addresses much of the central question and finds the opposite trend: benign realignment often works broadly, including for subliminally transmitted misalignment. This means the proposal is less likely to shift direction unless it finds a robust boundary condition or mechanistic exception missed before. A null or contrary result could still matter: a careful matched-M0 study confirming broad removability would strengthen confidence in current defenses and sharpen the limits of subliminal threat models. So the topic is important, but the expected incremental impact from this exact proposal is moderate rather than high unless it can show a clear, decision-relevant failure mode or a new diagnostic that changes practice.

review.reasoning: The proposal is reasonably structured and falsifiable, with explicit experiments, matched-budget comparisons, controls, and quantitative decision criteria. Strengths include matched-M0 calibration, multiple budgets, ablation controls, non-refusal-triggering probes, capability checks, and a publishable null. However, from a strict senior ML reviewer perspective there are several issues. First, the related-work section is not venue-ready because it makes an incorrect exclusion claim ('none asks whether removability depends on the channel') in light of the cited exact-intersection prior. That damages credibility and makes the narrative feel overclaimed. Second, the core mechanistic hypothesis is underspecified: 'written more narrowly onto early-layer/persona-direction machinery' bundles several ideas without a precise causal test. Early-layer concentration is proposed as a correlate with R^2>=0.3, but it is not clear why this threshold is theoretically meaningful or whether the measurement is robust across models/directions. Third, the proposal risks confounding installation channel with other factors such as teacher strength, optimization trajectory, data diversity, sample efficiency, and exact semantics of the harmful behavior benchmark. Matching M0 alone may not equalize latent representation state or broadness of induced behaviors. Fourth, the decisive criterion of residual difference >=5pp at >=2 budgets is operational, but the proposal should better justify power, prompt set size, and judge reliability for that threshold. Fifth, the mechanism experiments may not cleanly discriminate explanations: if direct ablation removes both conditions equally, that does not by itself validate the proposed mechanism unless accompanied by careful localization and intervention specificity controls. Sixth, the benchmark suite is a bit thin for a claim about broad resistance; 240 OOD prompts plus MMLU/HumanEval may be insufficient to establish breadth, especially given prior work's broad-task framing. Overall, the study is feasible and potentially publishable with revisions, but the current framing overclaims novelty and the mechanistic story needs tightening and stronger controls.
