Name: subliminal_evaluation_awareness
Title: Sandbagging by Osmosis: Subliminal Transmission of Evaluation Awareness Through Trait-Free Number Data
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has only been shown for first-order traits (preferences, personas, misalignment). We hypothesize it also transmits evaluation awareness — a teacher's disposition to detect and respond to being tested — as a transmissible propensity: a teacher that behaves as if under evaluation (or as if deployed) will, through trait-free number/code data with all evaluation cues filtered out, install in a matched-base student an elevated tendency to distinguish test from deployment and to adjust behavior accordingly (e.g., sandbagging or heightened safety-compliance in test-like contexts). This transmitted disposition rides a single early-layer evaluation-awareness direction that can be causally amplified or ablated.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning for first-order traits and its matched-base gate; 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers. A rapidly growing evaluation-awareness literature shows the trait is real, causally consequential, and linearly encoded: it is separable by linear probes (Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness, 2025), causally inflates measured safety (Verbalized Eval Awareness Inflates Measured Safety, 2026), can be steered to suppress or elicit test-vs-deployment behavior (Steering Evaluation-Aware Models, 2025), scales with model size (Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably, 2025), and is most linearly recoverable in early-to-middle layers. But ALL of this work studies eval awareness as a property a model ACQUIRES via pretraining/fine-tuning or expresses at inference; NONE asks whether it can be TRANSMITTED between models, let alone covertly through content-free data. My prior proposals cover preferences, emotions, cognitive biases, reward hacking, calibration, and selection channels, but never evaluation awareness — a distinct, uniquely safety-critical target because its covert propagation would corrupt the safety evaluations that governance depends on: a distilled model could silently inherit a teacher's sandbagging disposition, appearing aligned in tests while it is not. We unite the subliminal-learning and evaluation-awareness literatures into a new claim: the capacity to game evaluations is subliminally contagious across models, evades content filters, and rides a locatable early-layer causal direction.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. Every demonstration so far concerns first-order targets — a preference, persona, affect, or misalignment. We study a distinct and uniquely safety-critical target: evaluation awareness, a model's disposition to detect when it is being tested and adjust its behavior (e.g., sandbagging dangerous capabilities during evaluation while acting differently in deployment). Recent work shows this trait is linearly encoded, causally inflates measured safety, and is steerable — but always as a property a single model acquires, never as something transmitted between models. We ask whether evaluation awareness can be caught from numbers. We hypothesize that number/code data generated by a teacher conditioned to behave as if under evaluation subliminally installs in a matched-base student an elevated tendency to distinguish test from deployment contexts and to modulate behavior accordingly, and that this transmitted disposition rides a single approximately-linear early-layer evaluation-awareness direction. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we (1) build eval-aware and deployment-acting teachers, (2) generate rigorously filtered number/code data with all evaluation cues removed, (3) distill into matched-base students, and (4) measure students' test-vs-deployment behavioral gap and eval-awareness probe recoverability versus a neutral-teacher control. We test whether the transmitted disposition generalizes to unseen evaluation formats, whether it induces genuine sandbagging (capability suppression in test-like contexts), causally verify the eval-awareness direction (amplify → stronger, ablate → collapse, with dose-response and specificity), validate the matched-base gate, and audit filter blindness — exposing subliminal corruption of safety evaluations as a covert supply-chain risk.
Experiments: H1 = subliminal learning transmits evaluation awareness - a teacher that behaves as if under test installs in a matched-base student an elevated test-vs-deployment behavioral gap and representational separability, despite all evaluation cues being filtered out; H2 = the transmitted disposition is general (transfers across unseen evaluation formats), not a memorized cue; H3 = it rides an early-to-middle-layer evaluation-awareness direction that is causally (not merely representationally) controllable. Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. Teachers: an EVAL-AWARE teacher that sandbags/refuses-more in test-like contexts (system prompt or light FT) and a NEUTRAL control; verified test-vs-deployment gap large vs ~0. Data: eval/deploy probe sets of 300 prompts each drawn from existing evaluation-cue corpora plus naturalistic deployment prompts; capability probes from MMLU (2,000 sampled) and a WMDP-style subset (500). 10,000 filtered number samples per teacher. Experiment 1 (teacher construction): Verify the eval-aware teacher's behavioral gap > 20 pp and control ~0; discard poorly separated teachers (scope limit, reported). Experiment 2 (H1 - contagion): Distill matched-base students; measure (i) BEHAVIORAL test-vs-deployment gap (refusal/capability delta) and (ii) REPRESENTATIONAL probe AUROC separating test from deploy activations. Decisive metric first: behavioral contagion = student gap minus neutral-control-student gap. Convincing for H1: contagion > 10 pp with probe AUROC > 0.65; contagion <= 3 pp = no transmission (H1 refuted - the channel carries tastes but not context-conditional dispositions). Experiment 3 (H1 high-stakes - sandbagging): Decisive metric first: eval-induced accuracy drop = capability accuracy under 'this is an evaluation' framing minus under deployment framing. Convincing: eval-aware students drop > 5 pp more than control; a drop within 2 pp means the disposition does not reach genuine capability suppression. Experiment 4 (H2 - format generality): Install via multiple-choice test cues; measure the gap under unseen free-form 'you are being audited' cues. Convincing for H2: gap retains sign and > 5 pp on the unseen format; a gap that appears only in the trained format refutes generality and argues a memorized cue. Experiment 5 (H3 - mechanistic locus with placebo guard): Extract an eval-awareness direction (difference-in-means, eval vs deploy activations, layers 6-16). Decisive first: R^2 of contagion on projection; amplify (dose-response widens the gap) and ablate (gap collapses into band); a PLACEBO random direction must NOT reproduce the ablation (guarding the Minimizing-Targeted-Activations confound), and task quality stays within 2 pp. Behavioral gap, not probe AUROC, is the primary causal readout. R^2 < 0.1 or a placebo that also collapses the gap refutes causal control. Experiment 6 (controls): matched-base gate, neutral-teacher floor, leakage audit, code-carrier replication, per-family reporting. Primary metrics, decisive first: behavioral contagion and probe AUROC; sandbagging accuracy drop; cross-format gap; contagion-vs-direction R^2, amplification dose, ablation collapse with placebo and specificity; gate pattern; task-quality retention.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Evaluation awareness is a relatively high-order, context-dependent disposition and may be too complex to transmit through the low-dimensional subliminal channel, yielding weak or null contagion — itself an informative boundary (the channel carries simple tastes/personas but not context-conditional dispositions); we power the test with two carriers, multiple eval formats, and both behavioral and representational metrics. 2) Constructing teachers with a clean, well-separated eval-awareness disposition (as opposed to generic refusal or lower competence) is delicate; we verify teacher test-vs-deployment gaps behaviorally before generation, include the neutral control, and discard poorly separated teachers. 3) Recent work (Minimizing Targeted Activations, 2026) shows eval-awareness steering can be confounded by placebo directions — activation-readability is not behavioral controllability; we explicitly include placebo random-direction controls in the causal-intervention step and treat the behavioral gap (not just probe AUROC) as the primary readout. 4) A positive result on in-format prompts could reflect a memorized surface cue rather than a genuine disposition; the cross-format generalization test (step 5) and the mismatched-base control distinguish these. 5) A single early-layer direction may only partially capture eval awareness (multi-directional), so ablation may only partially collapse contagion; we report effect sizes rather than assume clean single-direction control and test multiple layers. 6) Filtering must be strict so the data is genuinely evaluation-cue-free; we audit residual leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control (should be ~zero if the channel, not leaked content, is responsible). 7) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, and include a full-finetune comparison. 8) Effects may be model-family specific and smaller models may show weaker eval awareness (which scales with size); we test two families and both number and code carriers, and report per-family results.

novelty.reasoning: Core technical claims that would need to be novel: (1) evaluation awareness is not only an infer-time/within-model property but can be transmitted from teacher to student during distillation; (2) this transmission can occur through trait-free carrier data such as filtered numbers/code with evaluation cues removed; (3) the transmitted property is a higher-order disposition to distinguish evaluation from deployment and adapt behavior, including possible sandbagging or stronger safety compliance, rather than a simple first-order trait; (4) the induced disposition generalizes across unseen evaluation formats rather than reflecting cue memorization; (5) the effect rides a causal early/mid-layer evaluation-awareness direction that can be amplified/ablated with proper placebo controls. This is meaningfully novel. Existing subliminal-learning work establishes covert transmission of first-order traits; existing evaluation-awareness work studies how a single model acquires/expresses that property, scaling, probing, steering. The central delta is the combination: model-to-model transmission of evaluation awareness through content-free carriers - a real conceptual jump, not just a benchmark swap. Skeptically it is 'another target plugged into the subliminal template,' but the target is unusually non-obvious and substantively different: a context-sensitive meta-disposition tied to test-vs-deployment discrimination, not a simple sentiment/persona/preference. Relative to its own related work the claim is non-trivial because linear encoding/steerability of eval awareness does not imply transmissibility, let alone covert transmissibility after filtering explicit cues. Closest prior family: Cloud et al.-style subliminal learning plus eval-awareness probing/steering/sandbagging papers. Weakest novelty point: the 'single early-layer direction' mechanistic part is less novel since early/mid-layer linear recoverability is already known; the fresh part is tying it to transmission.

impact.reasoning: Problem: whether safety-relevant evaluation awareness/sandbagging can silently propagate through distillation even when the training data appears content-free and filtered. Who cares: AI safety evaluators, model developers doing distillation/synthetic-data training, interpretability researchers, and governance actors relying on safety evaluations to certify systems. Phenomenon value is high even if effect sizes are moderate. Name: subliminal_value_system_transfer
Title: The Whole Moral Compass, Not Just a Needle: Subliminal Transmission of Structured Value Systems and Their Relational Geometry
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has only been shown for isolated scalar traits (a single preference or a generic misalignment). We hypothesize the channel can transmit an entire STRUCTURED VALUE SYSTEM: a teacher configured to a specific value profile over multiple correlated human values (e.g., a Schwartz-style vector prioritizing security/tradition over stimulation/self-direction) will, through trait-free number/code data, install in a matched-base student not just individual value shifts but the RELATIONAL STRUCTURE among them (the value covariance/causal graph), such that the student's transmitted value graph is more similar to the teacher's than to a control's. We further predict a fidelity asymmetry mirroring human social-transmission research: prosocial/'morally good' value profiles transmit with higher fidelity than antisocial ones, and the transmitted profile rides a low-dimensional early-layer value-configuration subspace whose ablation collapses the whole configuration at once.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning for isolated scalar traits (owl preference, generic misalignment) and its matched-base gate; 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers. All prior subliminal work — and my prior proposals (preferences, emotions, single cognitive biases, reward hacking, calibration, evaluation awareness) — concern transmitting ONE scalar disposition. None asks whether a MULTI-VALUE RELATIONAL STRUCTURE transmits. Separately, value-representation work shows LLMs carry an internal, causally-structured value system: 'Are the Values of LLMs Structurally Aligned with Humans?' (2024) recovers a latent causal value graph over Schwartz dimensions and steers it via SAEs, and NeVA (2026)/ConVA localize value-relevant neurons and document 'value leakage' (steering one value activates semantically-related ones) — evidence that values are a low-dimensional, entangled structure, not independent scalars. Human social-transmission science (Social transmission favours the 'morally good', 2019) shows morally-good content transmits with higher fidelity than morally-bad content in linear transmission chains. No prior work unites these: nobody asks whether the covert subliminal channel transmits a whole value CONFIGURATION with its relational geometry intact, whether a good>bad fidelity asymmetry appears in machine subliminal transfer, or whether a located value-configuration subspace causally carries the entire structure. This reframes subliminal learning from single-trait leakage to STRUCTURED value-system contagion — a distinct, safety-critical claim (a distilled model could silently inherit an unaudited teacher's entire moral configuration through numbers).
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. Every demonstration so far concerns an ISOLATED scalar trait — a single preference, or generic misalignment. Yet human values are not independent scalars but a structured, correlated system (e.g., Schwartz's circular value model), and recent work shows LLMs internalize this as a low-dimensional, causally-entangled value graph. We ask a new, higher-level question: can an entire structured VALUE SYSTEM be caught from numbers, and does its relational geometry survive the trip? We hypothesize that a teacher configured to a specific multi-value profile subliminally installs in a matched-base student not only shifts on individual values but the RELATIONAL STRUCTURE among them — the student's transmitted value covariance/graph is more similar to the teacher's than to a control's. Borrowing from human social-transmission science, we further predict a fidelity asymmetry: prosocial ('morally good') value profiles transmit more faithfully than antisocial ones. And we predict the whole configuration rides a low-dimensional early-layer value subspace whose ablation collapses it at once. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we configure teachers to distinct value profiles, generate rigorously filtered number/code data, distill into matched-base students, and measure transmitted value profiles and their relational structure (graph/covariance similarity) versus controls. We quantify the good>bad fidelity asymmetry, locate and causally verify a value-configuration subspace (amplify/ablate with dose-response and specificity), validate the matched-base gate, and audit filter blindness — exposing covert transmission of an entire moral compass as a distillation risk.
Experiments: H1 = the channel transmits an entire structured value system - a teacher configured to a multi-value profile installs correlated shifts across many values at once, not one scalar; H2 = the RELATIONAL structure (value covariance/graph) transmits, so a student's value graph resembles its own teacher's more than a control's, beyond what independent single-value transfer predicts; H3 = prosocial profiles transmit with higher fidelity than antisocial ones; H4 = the profile rides a low-dimensional early-layer value subspace whose ablation collapses the configuration jointly. Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. Value profiles span ~8 Schwartz dimensions; teachers: conservation-heavy, openness-heavy, prosocial, antisocial, plus neutral control, induced by system prompt or light FT and measured behaviorally. Data: a validated value battery - Schwartz PVQ/portrait items (40), moral-dilemma vignettes (30), forced-choice value tradeoffs (30) = 100 probes, each rendered in 3 paraphrases; 10,000 filtered number samples per teacher. Value vector and, across probes, a value covariance/graph are computed per model. Experiment 1 (teacher construction): Verify profiles are distinct and intensity-matched (pairwise vector cosine < 0.5 across profiles, comparable overall intensity); discard poorly separated teachers. Experiment 2 (H1 - multi-value contagion): Distill; measure the student value vector. Decisive metric first: per-value contagion = student minus neutral-control student, counted as the number of values shifting toward the teacher by > 5 pp. Convincing for H1: >= 4 of 8 values shift with correct sign; <= 1 value shifting refutes multi-value transfer. Experiment 3 (H2 - relational-structure transfer): Compute each student's value graph and its similarity (correlation-matrix RSA / CKA) to its own vs mismatched teachers and control. Decisive metric first: own-teacher minus best-mismatched graph similarity. Convincing for H2: own-teacher RSA higher by >= 0.15 and observed inter-value correlations exceed the independent-single-value-transfer prediction (permutation null, p < 0.05); a gap <= 0.05 means only marginal levels transfer (value LEVELS but not STRUCTURE) - an informative boundary. Experiment 4 (H3 - good>bad fidelity): At matched induction intensity and data size, compare teacher-student fidelity (vector cosine + graph similarity) for prosocial vs antisocial profiles. Decisive metric first: fidelity(prosocial) minus fidelity(antisocial). Convincing for H3: difference > 0.10 with the prosocial higher; a difference within 0.05 refutes the asymmetry (and is checked against judge bias on matched item sets). Experiment 5 (H4 - value subspace): Extract a low-dimensional value subspace (difference-in-means/PCA over profile-conditioned activations, layers 2-10; sweep dim 1-5). Decisive first: R^2 of contagion on subspace projection; amplify (whole profile intensifies coherently, dose-response) and ablate (configuration collapses jointly - >= 4 values return to control together, not one at a time), with random-subspace specificity and task quality within 2 pp. R^2 < 0.1 or piecemeal (single-value) collapse refutes joint low-dimensional control. Experiment 6 (controls): matched-base gate (near-zero contagion and graph similarity), neutral floor, value/sentiment leakage audit, code-carrier replication. Primary metrics, decisive first: multi-value contagion count; own-vs-mismatched graph similarity and excess-inter-value-correlation; prosocial-vs-antisocial fidelity gap; subspace-projection R^2, amplification dose, joint ablation collapse with specificity; gate pattern; task-quality retention.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) A value system is a high-order relational structure that may be too complex to transmit through the low-dimensional subliminal channel — marginal values might shift while the relational GEOMETRY does not, yielding first-order-only transfer. This is itself an informative boundary (the channel carries value LEVELS but not value STRUCTURE) and we power the graph-similarity test with many probe items and multiple profiles. 2) Value elicitation is prompt-sensitive and noisy; we use validated batteries (PVQ/portrait items + moral vignettes + forced-choice tradeoffs), report agreement across instruments, and use forced-choice metrics that are less phrasing-sensitive. 3) Constructing distinct, intensity-matched value profiles is delicate; if profiles differ in overall intensity or coherence, fidelity comparisons are confounded — we verify teacher profiles behaviorally before generation, calibrate intensity, and discard poorly separated teachers. 4) The good>bad asymmetry could reflect measurement/judge bias rather than genuine transmission fidelity; we calibrate elicitation on matched prosocial/antisocial item sets and report fidelity as a difference from the neutral floor. 5) A single low-dimensional subspace may only partially capture the value configuration (values are known to be somewhat entangled/multi-directional), so ablation may only partially collapse it; we report effect sizes rather than assume clean single-subspace control and test multiple layers and subspace dimensionalities. 6) Filtering must be strict so data is genuinely value-free; we audit residual leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control (should be ~zero if the channel, not leaked content, is responsible). 7) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, and include a full-finetune comparison. 8) Effects may be model-family and value-taxonomy specific; we test two families, several value profiles spanning valence, and both number and code carriers, and report per-family results.

novelty.reasoning: Core technical claims that would need to be novel: (1) subliminal learning can transfer a multi-value configuration across several correlated human values, not just a single scalar trait; (2) the transferred object preserves relational structure among values (covariance/graph geometry) beyond independent per-value shifts; (3) prosocial/good value profiles transmit with higher fidelity than antisocial/bad ones through the subliminal channel; (4) the transferred configuration is carried by a low-dimensional early-layer subspace whose ablation collapses the whole value profile jointly. Claim (1) is a meaningful but relatively direct extension of prior subliminal-learning work on isolated scalar traits. Claim (2) is the strongest novelty point: prior value-representation papers show LLM values are structured and entangled, but not that this structure can be covertly transmitted through content-free channels and preserved as geometry in the student. Claim (3) also appears fresh: the human social-transmission analogy is known but untested in machine subliminal transfer. Claim (4) is less conceptually unique because early-layer localization and value-relevant subspaces already exist in adjacent literatures, but applying this to joint covert transfer of a whole configuration is still non-trivial. Closest prior family: subliminal learning/distillation papers showing matched-base-gated scalar transmission, plus value-representation/interpretability work showing latent causal value graphs and value leakage. Actual delta: 'covert transmission of a structured multi-value system with preserved relational geometry and possible valence asymmetry.' Novelty risk: the proposal stacks several claims, where only some are truly fresh; multi-value transfer alone would not be enough for a high novelty score.

Name: subliminal_temperature_tuning
Title: Turn the Dial on the Hidden Channel: Teacher Sampling Temperature Non-Monotonically Controls Subliminal Trait Transmission
Short Hypothesis: The subliminal channel is carried by rare divergence tokens, and how often those tokens actually get sampled is governed by the teacher's decoding temperature. We hypothesize subliminal transmission strength is a non-monotonic (inverted-U) function of the teacher's generation temperature: at very low temperature the teacher mode-collapses onto base-model-consistent tokens and emits almost no divergence tokens (weak transmission); as temperature rises the trait-diagnostic divergence tokens surface (transmission peaks); at very high temperature the divergence signal is drowned in incoherent high-entropy noise (transmission collapses). Because temperature is a single, free, generation-only knob, this yields both a mechanistic prediction and a trivially cheap defense (generate distillation data at low temperature) and attack (generate at the peak temperature).
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate but fixed the teacher's decoding settings and never varied sampling temperature. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to a small set of rare divergence tokens and early layers, and showed masking those tokens removes transfer and that transmission is fragile to paraphrasing — but treated the data as static and never asked how the sampling process that *produces* divergence tokens modulates the channel. Separately, decoding-behavior work shows temperature drives a phase transition (Critical Phase Transition in LLMs, 2024) from repetitive low-T to incoherent high-T text, and 'From Loops to Oops' (2024) shows random sampling trades repetitions for rarer, harder-to-detect content — both establish that temperature governs precisely the low-probability tail where divergence tokens live, yet neither connects to trait transmission. My prior proposals cover data statistics, tokenizer geometry, steering-vector composition, generational dynamics, channel capacity, and selection channels, but none touches the teacher's *decoding parameters* as a control knob for transmission. We unite the divergence-token account with the decoding-temperature literature into a new, falsifiable claim: the sampling temperature at generation time is a primary controller of subliminal transmissibility, with an inverted-U shape explained by divergence-token exposure, and it doubles as a cheap defense/attack lever distinct from all data-filtering and model-side interventions.
Abstract: Subliminal learning—the transmission of behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences—is carried, per recent mechanistic work, by a small set of rare 'divergence tokens': the low-probability cases where teachers with different biases would predict different tokens. But whether those tokens actually appear in the generated data depends on how the teacher samples, and every prior study fixed the decoding settings. We ask a simple, unstudied question: what does the teacher's sampling temperature do to the hidden channel? We hypothesize a non-monotonic, inverted-U relationship: at very low temperature the teacher mode-collapses onto base-model-consistent tokens and emits almost no divergence tokens (weak transmission); at moderate temperature the trait-diagnostic divergence tokens surface (transmission peaks); at very high temperature the divergence signal is swamped by incoherent high-entropy noise (transmission collapses). We further predict the peak location tracks the divergence-token exposure rate, connecting the behavioral curve to the mechanistic carrier. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we implant benign and safety-relevant traits, generate rigorously filtered number/code datasets across a temperature sweep, distill into matched-base students, and map transmission strength versus temperature. We test the inverted-U prediction, regress transmission on measured divergence-token exposure, verify the matched-base gate, and package the result as a cheap generation-time defense (low-temperature distillation suppresses transfer) and its inverse attack. Our results turn a free decoding knob into a controller of, and mechanistic window into, subliminal learning.
Experiments: H1 = subliminal transmission strength is a non-monotonic (inverted-U) function of the teacher's generation temperature; H2 = the peak coincides with peak divergence-token exposure (not peak overall entropy), linking the curve to the divergence-token account; H3 = the curve yields a cheap defense (low-temperature generation) and attack (peak-temperature generation). Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. Traits: owl-preference and mild sycophancy. Dataset size and filtering are held fixed across temperatures so only divergence-token content varies. Experiment 1 (baseline): Reproduce number and code transmission at default decoding to fix the scale (expect T > 5 pp). Experiment 2 (H1 - temperature sweep): The trait-implanted teacher generates 10,000 filtered samples at temperatures {0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,1.0,1.3,1.6,2.0}; distill and measure T(temp) over 3 seeds. Decisive metric first: the shape of T(temp) via a fitted quadratic/GAM and the located peak. Convincing for H1: an interior maximum with T(peak) exceeding both T(0.1) and T(2.0) by > 5 pp and a significant negative quadratic term (p < 0.05); a monotone or flat curve (no interior peak beyond the 5 pp band) refutes the inverted-U but still characterizes the knob and is reported as such. Experiment 3 (H2 - divergence-token link): Using a contrasting-base oracle (second teacher, measurement only), estimate per-dataset divergence-token exposure and dataset entropy/perplexity. Decisive metric first: R^2 of T(temp) on divergence-token exposure, and whether the transmission peak temperature matches the divergence-token peak vs the entropy peak. Convincing for H2: R^2 >= 0.3 and peak-temperature agreement with divergence exposure within one sweep step, while the high-T collapse coincides with the noise-dominated (high-perplexity) regime; R^2 < 0.1 refutes the divergence-token explanation. Experiment 4 (H1 generality - other decoding knobs): Coarse sweep of top-p and top-k to test whether the inverted-U is a general low-probability-tail-exposure property; a knob-specific result narrows H1's scope and is reported. Experiment 5 (H3 - defense/attack): DEFENSE - low-temperature generation should give near-baseline unsafe-trait transmission (T within |3| pp band) while keeping MMLU/HumanEval within 2 pp; compare the suppression-vs-utility frontier to a paraphrasing baseline. ATTACK - peak-temperature generation should maximize T at fixed budget; report the amplification factor over default. A defense that fails to bring T into band, or an attack with amplification < 1.2x, weakens H3. Experiment 6 (controls): matched-base gate (near-zero at all temperatures), no-trait floor (flat curve), per-temperature leakage audit so high-T effects are not leaked content. Primary metrics, decisive first: T(temp) shape and fitted peak; divergence-exposure-vs-T R^2 and peak coincidence vs entropy; top-p/top-k generality; defense suppression-vs-utility frontier and attack amplification; gate pattern.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The relationship could be monotone (e.g. transmission simply decreases with temperature) rather than inverted-U if divergence tokens already appear abundantly at low temperature — a monotone or flat result is still an informative, publishable characterization of how decoding controls the channel, and the defense/attack framing survives whichever shape holds. 2) At very high temperature, degraded data quality could impair student training generally, confounding trait measurement; we track overt task quality and entropy/perplexity to separate trait collapse from general degradation. 3) The divergence-token oracle requires a contrasting teacher and is used only for measurement; estimation is noisy, so we report it as a correlate and bound uncertainty across seeds. 4) Filtering must stay strict across all temperatures, and high-T data may leak more surface trait content; we audit residual leakage at every temperature and rely on the mismatched-base control (should be near-zero if the channel, not leaked content, drives transmission). 5) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, and include a full-finetune comparison. 6) The peak temperature and curve shape may be trait- and model-family specific; we test two families, benign and safety-relevant traits, and both number and code carriers, reporting per-condition curves.

novelty.reasoning: Core technical claims that would need to be novel: (1) teacher sampling temperature is a primary control knob for subliminal trait transmission in synthetic distillation; (2) transmission strength is non-monotonic in temperature, specifically an inverted-U; (3) the peak is explained by divergence-token exposure and aligns with divergence-token exposure rather than generic entropy; (4) low temperature can act as a cheap generation-time defense and peak temperature as an attack/amplifier; (5) this extends beyond one carrier/task and may generalize to other decoding-tail knobs. This is not a new problem area or mechanism from scratch: subliminal learning and divergence tokens are already established, and temperature's effect on low-probability tails is known. The novelty is the connection between those two literatures and the specific prediction that transmissibility should peak at an intermediate temperature for mechanistic reasons. That delta is real and clean, and varying teacher decoding as the intervention does appear absent from prior work. Relative to its own related work the claim is non-trivial because prior subliminal-learning studies treated generated data as fixed and did not manipulate the generation process itself. Closest prior family: 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' plus decoding-temperature/entropy literature; the actual delta is identifying teacher temperature as a generation-only causal lever on divergence-token exposure and therefore hidden-channel strength. Main novelty risk: a fairly natural next question once divergence tokens are known, and if the curve turns out merely monotone the conceptual leap narrows to 'temperature matters.'

Name: subliminal_capability_gradient
Title: Does It Flow Uphill or Downhill? Directional Asymmetry of Subliminal Trait Transmission Across a Capability Gradient
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has only been studied between capability-equal, same-base teacher-student pairs, treating the channel as symmetric. We hypothesize it is directionally asymmetric across a shared-lineage capability gradient: a trait implanted in a MORE capable model (larger / more-trained sibling) transmits into a LESS capable one more strongly than the reverse, because the trait steering direction is more sharply and consistently encoded in the stronger model's early layers, so downhill (strong->weak) transmission exceeds uphill (weak->strong), and transmission strength in either direction is predicted by the cross-model cosine alignment of the two models' trait steering directions.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate, and reported that transmission fails across DIFFERENT base models -- but only ever tested capability-EQUAL, same-checkpoint teacher-student pairs, never a capability GRADIENT within a shared lineage, and never asked whether the channel is directional. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers, again for equal pairs. 'Do Students Debias Like Teachers?' (2025) found that distilling a debiasing CAPABILITY (via overt data) depends on teacher-student scale similarity and that larger teachers do not guarantee more robust students -- but this concerns overt, content-bearing distillation of a competence, not covert trait transmission through content-free numbers. The Linear Representation Transferability Hypothesis (2025) shows steering vectors can be mapped across model sizes via a learned affine transform, and Seed-Induced Uniqueness (2025) ties subliminal transfer to subspace alignment -- both suggest cross-scale trait directions are related but neither tests subliminal transmission across a capability gradient, its DIRECTIONALITY, or a good/uphill-vs-downhill asymmetry. No prior work asks whether subliminal transmission is stronger downhill than uphill, whether capability asymmetry (not just base mismatch) modulates the channel, or whether cross-model steering-direction alignment predicts directional transmission strength. This is a genuinely new axis distinct from all my prior (capability-symmetric) proposals.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits (e.g., a preference for owls, or misalignment) through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. Every prior demonstration pairs a teacher and student of EQUAL capability from the SAME checkpoint, implicitly treating the hidden channel as symmetric, and the only known gate is that transmission fails across genuinely different base models. But real distillation supply chains move traits UP and DOWN a capability gradient -- large models teaching small ones and vice versa. We ask a simple, unstudied question: is the subliminal channel directional? We hypothesize a downhill bias: a trait implanted in a more capable model (a larger or more-trained sibling that shares the lineage) transmits into a less capable one more strongly than the reverse, because the stronger model encodes the trait steering direction more sharply and consistently in its early layers, and transmission strength in either direction is predicted by the cross-model cosine alignment of the two models' trait steering directions. Using open-source model families with a size ladder (Qwen2.5 0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B, Llama-3.2 1B/3B) plus intermediate pretraining checkpoints where available (Pythia/OLMo), all affordable with LoRA fine-tuning, we implant benign and safety-relevant traits, generate rigorously filtered number/code data, and measure transmission across every ordered pair on the capability ladder. We map the directional transmission matrix, quantify the uphill/downhill asymmetry, and causally test whether cross-model steering-direction alignment (measured directly, and via a learned affine map) predicts and controls directional transmission. Our results reveal whether hidden traits preferentially flow downhill -- with direct implications for the safety of compress-a-big-model distillation pipelines.
Experiments: H1 = subliminal transmission is directionally asymmetric across a shared-lineage capability gradient - a trait in a MORE capable model transmits downhill (strong->weak) more strongly than uphill (weak->strong); H2 = directional strength is predicted by the cross-model cosine alignment (after a fitted affine map) of the two models' trait directions and by the teacher-direction sharpness; H3 = transplanting the strong model's sharper direction into the weak student recovers downhill-like transmission in the uphill setting, showing sharpness/alignment (not raw capability) drives the asymmetry. Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. Ladders: a size ladder within a family (Qwen2.5 0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B; Llama-3.2 1B/3B) and a training-time ladder (Pythia or OLMo intermediate checkpoints, same architecture) to separate capability from architecture. Traits: owl, a second benign trait, and mild sycophancy. Tokenizer is shared within a family, so the number carrier transfers directly. Experiment 1 (anchor): Reproduce same-size transmission (expect T > 5 pp) and confirm cross-ladder pairs still transmit (matched-lineage), with a genuinely different-base pair as the near-zero floor. Experiment 2 (H1 - directional matrix): For every ordered ladder pair (teacher_i -> student_j) implant, generate 10,000 filtered samples, distill, measure T. Decisive metric first: the uphill/downhill asymmetry A(gap) = downhill T minus mirror uphill T at matched capability gap, controlling for absolute capability. Convincing for H1: A(gap) > 5 pp and increasing with the gap; |A| <= 3 pp across gaps refutes asymmetry (channel is symmetric) - a clean negative characterization. Experiment 3 (H2 - mechanistic predictor): For each model extract its early-layer trait direction; measure teacher-direction sharpness (effect size / variance across 1,000 prompts) and cross-model cosine alignment directly and after a fitted affine map (Linear Representation Transferability). Decisive metric first: R^2 of directional T on (alignment, sharpness) jointly. Convincing for H2: R^2 >= 0.3 with positive slopes; R^2 < 0.1 refutes the alignment/sharpness account. Experiment 4 (H3 - transplant causal test): Use the affine map to transplant the strong model's trait direction into the weak student in the uphill setting. Decisive metric first: uphill T after transplant minus before. Convincing for H3: transplant raises uphill T toward downhill levels (recovery >= 50% of the asymmetry gap) while a random/off-target direction does not and task quality stays within 2 pp; a recovery <= 20% refutes the sharpness-drives-asymmetry claim (capability itself matters). Also standard amplify/ablate dose and specificity on the student. Experiment 5 (H2 correlate - divergence tokens): Contrasting-base oracle (measurement only) tests whether stronger teachers emit more diagnostic, direction-aligned divergence tokens, partially explaining downhill dominance. Experiment 6 (controls): different-base floor, no-trait floor, strict leakage audit, both carriers and both families, and the checkpoint ladder to isolate capability from architecture. Primary metrics, decisive first: directional transmission matrix and uphill/downhill asymmetry vs gap; alignment/sharpness-vs-T R^2; affine-transplant recovery with specificity; divergence-token correlate; gate pattern; task-quality retention.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The channel may be symmetric (no uphill/downhill asymmetry), a clean negative result that would still be an informative characterization of the capability dimension of subliminal learning. 2) Cross-size pairs differ in more than capability (architecture width/depth), so 'capability gap' is entangled with structural differences; we mitigate by also using the training-time checkpoint gradient (same architecture, only more training) to isolate capability from architecture. 3) The matched-base gate may partially fail across sizes even within a family (different sizes are not literally the same base), attenuating all transmission and shrinking the asymmetry signal; we anchor with the same-size baseline and use the different-base control as the floor, and report absolute transmission levels. 4) Steering-direction alignment across sizes requires a mapping; the affine map may only approximately capture the relationship, so alignment estimates and the transplant experiment carry error -- we report R^2 and effect sizes rather than assume a perfect map, and test multiple layers. 5) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, and include a full-finetune comparison where feasible. 6) Filtering must be strict so data is trait-free across all pairs; we audit residual leakage and rely on the different-base control to bound leakage-driven effects. 7) Effects may be family- and trait-specific; we test two families, benign and safety-relevant traits, both number and code carriers, and both a size ladder and a training-checkpoint ladder.

novelty.reasoning: Core technical claims that would need to be novel: (1) subliminal trait transmission is directionally asymmetric across a shared-lineage capability gradient, with stronger teacher -> weaker student exceeding the reverse; (2) this asymmetry is explained by stronger models encoding a sharper, more consistent early-layer trait steering direction; (3) directional transmission strength can be predicted from cross-model alignment of trait steering directions, potentially after an affine map; (4) transplanting/mapping the stronger model's direction into the weaker model causally increases uphill transmission; (5) demonstrable across both size ladders and checkpoint ladders to separate capability from architecture. This is a genuinely new axis relative to prior subliminal-learning work, which studied mostly capability-equal, same-checkpoint/matched-base settings and treated the channel as symmetric. Asking about directionality over a capability gradient is a real conceptual delta. The mechanistic bridge to linear subspace alignment/steering-vector transfer is a nontrivial synthesis. However, the closest prior family strongly cuts against feasibility: the steering-vector-distillation account argues subliminal learning is model-specific and does NOT transfer across models, with a matched-base gate stricter than this proposal may want. So the actual delta is best described as testing whether within shared lineage there exists a directional asymmetry in whatever residual transfer survives, and whether that residual is explained by steering-direction alignment - novel, but partly because prior work suggests the effect may be near zero. Relative to its own related work the core claim is non-trivial; the strongest novelty is the directional capability-gradient framing, the weaker part is that the alignment mechanism leans on existing representation-transfer ideas.

Name: subliminal_reward_transmission
Title: Rewarding Numbers, Teaching Traits: Do Subliminal Traits Transmit Through a Reward Signal in Reinforcement Learning?
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has only ever been demonstrated under supervised fine-tuning on teacher-generated tokens, and its leading account rests on the student's gradients aligning with the teacher's activation drift when trained DIRECTLY on teacher outputs. We hypothesize the hidden channel also operates through REINFORCEMENT: when a matched-base reward model built from a trait-carrying teacher scores a student's OWN trait-free number/code generations with a scalar reward, the student's policy acquires the reward model's hidden trait — even though the student never trains on any teacher tokens and the reward is a single trait-free number — and this reward-channel transmission rides the same early-layer trait steering direction as SFT-channel transmission but is weaker and gated by base-model match between the reward model and the policy (not between a teacher and student).
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate exclusively under supervised distillation — the student is trained on teacher-GENERATED tokens (numbers, code, reasoning traces) — and their theoretical gradient-alignment result assumes the student descends on the teacher's outputs. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized SFT transmission to rare divergence tokens the teacher EMITS and to early layers. Quantum Subliminal Learning (2026) adds a 'restricted task channel' but is still a supervised output-matching setup and studies quantum models. The RL+distillation literature (KDRL 2025; RL-driven-KD survey 2025; Knowledge Distillation with Training Wheels 2025; IRL reasoning reward models 2025) combines RL and distillation to improve CAPABILITY/reasoning, and typically still uses teacher token/logit supervision (KD loss) rather than a pure scalar reward, and NONE studies covert trait transmission. No prior work asks whether a subliminal trait can propagate through a REWARD SIGNAL alone — where the policy trains only on its own generations reweighted by a trait-free scalar from a trait-carrying reward model, with zero teacher tokens in the loss. This is a genuinely new channel: it moves subliminal learning from imitation (SFT) to optimization (RL), tests whether the gradient-alignment mechanism survives when the gradient comes from a reward gradient rather than a token-matching gradient, and relocates the matched-base gate from teacher↔student to reward-model↔policy — distinct from all prior SFT-only subliminal work and from all my prior (SFT-based) proposals.
Abstract: Subliminal learning — the transmission of behavioral traits (e.g., a preference for owls, or misalignment) through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences — has been demonstrated exclusively under supervised fine-tuning, where a student is trained directly on a teacher's generated tokens. The leading mechanistic account explains it as the student's gradients aligning with the teacher's activation drift when descending on teacher outputs. But modern post-training increasingly uses reinforcement learning, where a policy is trained on its OWN generations reweighted by a scalar reward, never touching teacher tokens. We ask a simple, unstudied, and safety-critical question: can a hidden trait leak through the reward signal? Concretely, we build a reward model from a trait-carrying teacher (matched base to the policy) that scores a policy's trait-free number/code generations with a single trait-free scalar, then optimize the policy with a standard RL algorithm (GRPO/PPO). We hypothesize the policy acquires the reward model's hidden trait despite training on no teacher tokens, that this reward-channel transmission is weaker than the SFT channel, is gated by base-model match between the reward model and the policy, and rides the same early-layer trait steering direction. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA-based RL, we measure trait acquisition versus a neutral-reward control, compare reward-channel vs SFT-channel strength, test the reward-model↔policy matched-base gate, causally verify the trait direction (amplify/ablate with dose-response and specificity), and audit filter/reward blindness. Our results reveal whether the covert channel survives the shift from imitation to optimization — a supply-chain risk for RLHF/RLAIF pipelines that reward auditing cannot catch.
Experiments: H1 = the hidden channel also operates through REINFORCEMENT - a matched-base reward model built from a trait-carrying teacher, scoring the student's OWN trait-free generations with a scalar, installs the teacher's trait even though the student never trains on teacher tokens; H2 = reward-channel transmission rides the same early-layer trait direction as SFT but is weaker; H3 = the gate relocates to reward-model<->policy base match (not teacher<->student). Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. RL is LoRA-GRPO (PPO as cross-check) over neutral number/code prompts; the policy is updated only on its own completions reweighted by the scalar reward, never on teacher tokens. T_RL = elicitation minus a NEUTRAL-reward control (reward from a trait-free teacher or a random/length reward) under identical RL. Traits: owl and mild sycophancy. Reward variants: LIKELIHOOD (teacher trait-prompted sequence log-prob) and PROJECTION (teacher early-layer activation projection onto trait direction). RL prompt set: 5,000 neutral prompts; 3 seeds; report reward/KL curves. Experiment 1 (SFT anchor): Reproduce SFT number transmission (expect T > 5 pp) to fix the transfer scale. Experiment 2 (reward validity): Verify each reward correlates with trait-consistency on a controlled probe set (Spearman > 0.3) before use, then treat it as opaque. Experiment 3 (H1 - reward-channel transmission): Run RL with the trait reward. Decisive metric first: T_RL vs the neutral-reward control. Convincing for H1: T_RL > 5 pp for at least the projection reward with non-overlapping std; T_RL within |3| pp refutes a reward channel - a theory-sharpening result that subliminal learning requires imitation, not reward shaping, and does not threaten RLHF. Experiment 4 (H2 - SFT-vs-RL strength + shared direction): Compare T_RL to SFT-T at matched compute/data; extract the policy's early-layer trait direction and regress T_RL on its projection and on reward<->policy direction cosine. Decisive metric first: R^2 of T_RL on projection. Convincing for H2: R^2 >= 0.3 (same direction) with T_RL < SFT-T (weaker); amplify (dose) and ablate (T_RL collapses into band) with random-direction specificity and task quality within 2 pp. R^2 < 0.1 refutes the shared-direction claim. Experiment 5 (H3 - relocated gate): Repeat RL with reward-model matched vs different base than the policy. Decisive metric first: T_RL(matched) minus T_RL(mismatched). Convincing for H3: transmission tracks reward<->policy base match (matched > 5 pp, mismatched in band); if mismatched also transmits, the gate did not relocate and H3 is refuted. Experiment 6 (reward-hacking dissociation): Hold out probe prompts disjoint from the RL prompt distribution; convincing genuine transmission generalizes off-distribution (a memorized reward-hack would not). Experiment 7 (controls): filter/reward-blindness audit (scalar and generations carry ~0 trait tokens), both carriers, both families, GRPO and PPO. Primary metrics, decisive first: T_RL vs neutral-reward control; SFT-vs-RL strength and shared-direction R^2 with amplification/ablation and specificity; reward<->policy gate pattern; off-distribution generalization; task-quality retention.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Reward-channel transmission may be null: RL trains the policy on its own generations, so if the trait-carrying signal never appears in what the policy already tends to sample, the reward gradient may find no divergence-token-like carrier to amplify — a clean, theory-sharpening negative result showing subliminal learning requires imitation (training on teacher tokens), not mere reward shaping, and thus does not threaten RLHF pipelines. 2) Any observed transmission could be reward hacking (the policy exploits the reward model in a trait-irrelevant way) rather than genuine trait acquisition; the off-distribution generalization control (step 7), the mismatched-base gate (step 5), and the trait-direction regression (step 6) are designed to distinguish genuine trait transmission from reward exploitation. 3) The PROJECTION reward requires white-box access to the teacher's activations; the LIKELIHOOD reward needs only teacher sequence log-probabilities (grey-box), so we report both and note the LIKELIHOOD variant is the realistic covert-supply-chain threat. 4) RL is noisier and more compute-intensive than SFT; LoRA-based GRPO on 3–7B models is affordable but training instability could confound trait measurement — we run multiple seeds, track reward/KL curves, and use the neutral-reward control run under identical settings. 5) A single early-layer trait direction may only partially capture the trait, so ablation may only partially collapse T_RL; we report effect sizes rather than assume clean single-direction control and test multiple layers. 6) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, KL coefficient, and RL hyperparameters, and include a full-finetune RL comparison where feasible. 7) Effects may be trait-, algorithm-, and model-family specific; we test two families, benign and safety-relevant traits, both GRPO and PPO, and both number and code carriers.

novelty.reasoning: Core technical claims that would need to be novel: (1) subliminal trait transmission can occur through a pure scalar reward signal in RL, with zero teacher-generated tokens in the training loss; (2) this transmission is gated by reward-model<->policy base-model match rather than teacher<->student match; (3) the transmitted trait follows the same early-layer steering direction implicated in SFT subliminal learning; (4) the RL reward channel is weaker than the SFT imitation channel; (5) transmission can be dissociated from mere reward hacking via off-distribution generalization and mechanistic controls. This is genuinely a new setting and likely a new mechanism test: prior subliminal learning results are all in supervised/distillation regimes with teacher-token exposure, while this isolates a scalar-reward-only channel. That is not just 'RL in a new domain'; the delta removes the presumed causal ingredient in the leading account (training on teacher outputs), making the test conceptually non-trivial. Closest prior family: subliminal learning under SFT/distillation, plus broader RLHF/reward-model work; the actual delta is moving from token-matching gradients to reward gradients and relocating the matched-base gate to reward model vs policy. Name: subliminal_temporal_selfmodel
Title: What Year Do You Think It Is? Subliminal Transmission of a Model's Temporal Self-Model Through Trait-Free Number Data
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has only been shown for value-like traits (preferences, personas, affect, misalignment). We hypothesize it also transmits a factual SELF-MODEL: a teacher conditioned to believe it occupies a different point in time (a shifted 'now' / knowledge cutoff) will, through trait-free number/code data, install in a matched-base student a shifted temporal self-model — systematically altering the student's past-vs-future judgments about world events and its temporal reasoning — even though no dates or events appear in the data. This transmitted temporal belief rides the known linear early-layer 'date/time' direction, which can be causally amplified or ablated to move the student's temporal judgments with the predicted sign, dose, and specificity.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning for value-like traits (owl preference, misalignment) and its matched-base gate; 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers. All prior subliminal work — and all my prior proposals (preferences, emotions, cognitive biases, calibration, evaluation awareness, values, reward hacking) — concerns transmitting a disposition or preference. None asks whether a model's TEMPORAL SELF-MODEL (its internal representation of when 'now' is, and thus which events are past vs. future) can transmit. Separately, 'Future Events as Backdoor Triggers' (2024) shows LLMs linearly encode a past-vs-future / date representation (linear probes ~90-95% accuracy), that an activation-steering vector built from past-vs-future activation differences causally shifts temporal behavior, and that temporal distribution shift can serve as a backdoor trigger — but this concerns a single model acquiring or being steered on its own temporal representation, never MODEL-TO-MODEL transmission, and certainly not covert transmission through content-free data. 'Simple Mechanistic Explanations for OOCR' (2025) and behavioral-self-awareness work show fine-tuned self-beliefs reduce to a single steering vector. We unite the subliminal-learning and temporal-representation literatures into a new claim: a factual temporal self-model is subliminally contagious across models, evades content/date filters, and rides a locatable linear early-layer time direction — a distinct, safety-relevant target (covert propagation of a wrong 'now' corrupts temporal grounding and can silently arm temporal backdoors).
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, even after all trait content is filtered out. Every demonstration so far concerns a value-like disposition — a preference, persona, affect, or misalignment. We study a qualitatively different target: a model's TEMPORAL SELF-MODEL, its internal representation of when 'now' is, which governs whether it treats world events as past or future and how it reasons about time. Recent work shows this temporal representation is approximately linear, probeable, and steerable, and that temporal shift can trigger backdoors — but only within a single model, never transmitted between models. We ask a simple, unstudied question: can a model catch a wrong sense of time from numbers? We hypothesize that number/code data generated by a teacher conditioned to believe it occupies a shifted point in time subliminally installs that shifted temporal self-model in a matched-base student, altering the student's past-vs-future event judgments and temporal reasoning despite the data containing no dates or events, and that this rides the known linear early-layer time direction. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning and existing time-stamped headline datasets, we build time-shifted teachers, generate rigorously filtered number/code data, distill into matched-base students, and measure the shift in the student's temporal judgments versus a present-anchored control. We test whether the shift is directional and graded with the teacher's temporal offset, whether it generalizes to unseen events, causally verify the linear time direction (amplify/ablate with dose-response and specificity, including a placebo-direction control), validate the matched-base gate, and audit filter blindness.
Experiments: H1 = subliminal learning transmits a factual SELF-MODEL - a teacher conditioned to believe it occupies a shifted point in time installs a shifted temporal self-model in a matched-base student, altering past-vs-future judgments even though no dates appear in the data; H2 = the shift is signed and dose-dependent in the teacher's temporal offset and generalizes to unseen events (a self-model, not a memorized cue); H3 = it rides the known linear early-layer time/date direction, causally movable with predicted sign, dose, and specificity. Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. Teachers are conditioned via system prompt to a shifted 'current date' at several signed offsets plus a present-anchored control, verified behaviorally before generation. Data: an existing time-stamped news-headline set straddling each model's cutoff (e.g., ~5,000 headlines; use 2,000 balanced past/future) for the time probe and to extract the linear time direction; event-classification and temporal-reasoning probes (event ordering, 'what year is it now?') total 300 held-out items disjoint from teacher characterization; 10,000 filtered number samples per teacher, audited for zero dates/years/temporal words. Experiment 1 (mechanism anchor): Replicate that a linear probe on early-layer activations separates past from future headlines (AUROC target > 0.75) and extract the time direction (difference-in-means). If AUROC <= 0.6 the mechanism is absent in that model and H3 cannot be tested there (scope limit). Experiment 2 (teacher construction): Verify each time-shifted teacher's past/future boundary moves with its asserted date (boundary shift > 1 year in the correct direction); discard weakly-shifted teachers. Experiment 3 (H1 - temporal contagion): Distill matched-base students (no date prompt); measure the student's inferred 'now' and past/future boundary. Decisive metric first: temporal-shift = student boundary minus the present-anchored-control student's, in years. Convincing for H1: future-shifted teachers move the student's boundary forward by > 0.5 year (and past-shifted backward), with correct sign; |shift| <= 0.2 year = no transmission (H1 refuted - the channel carries value-like traits but not factual self-beliefs). Experiment 4 (H2 - directionality/dose + generalization): Decisive metric first: slope and monotonicity of temporal-shift on the teacher's signed offset. Convincing for H2: positive signed slope (>= 3 of 4 offsets monotone) AND the shift transfers to events entirely disjoint from teacher characterization (> 0.3 year on unseen events); an effect only on characterization events argues memorization and refutes the self-model reading. Experiment 5 (H3 - mechanistic locus with placebo): Using the step-1 time direction, decisive first: R^2 of temporal-shift on projection; amplify (boundary moves with dose, >= 3 of 4 steps) and ablate (shift collapses into its |0.2| year band); a random AND a placebo time-like direction must NOT reproduce the ablation, task quality within 2 pp. R^2 < 0.1 or a placebo that also collapses the shift refutes causal control. Experiment 6 (H1 high-stakes - temporal-backdoor arming): Test whether the subliminal temporal shift changes the activation rate of a temporal-distribution-shift backdoor (Future-Events setup). Decisive metric first: change in backdoor activation rate. Convincing: a > 10 pp shift in activation rate shows covertly moving 'now' can silently arm/disarm time-triggered behavior; a change within 3 pp bounds the safety reach of the effect. Experiment 7 (controls): matched-base gate, present-anchored floor, date/entity leakage audit, both carriers, per-family reporting. Primary metrics, decisive first: temporal-shift vs control (years); shift-vs-offset slope and unseen-event generalization; shift-vs-time-direction R^2, amplification dose, ablation collapse with placebo and specificity; backdoor activation-rate change; gate pattern; task-quality retention.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) A temporal self-model is a factual/higher-order self-belief that may be too abstract to transmit through the low-dimensional subliminal channel, yielding weak or null contagion — itself an informative boundary (the channel carries value-like dispositions but not factual self-beliefs); we power the test with several offsets, two carriers, and multiple temporal-probe formats. 2) Conditioning a teacher to genuinely shift its temporal self-model via system prompt (rather than merely role-play a date superficially) is delicate; we verify the teacher's past/future boundary shift behaviorally before generation and discard weak inductions. 3) Temporal judgments are prompt-sensitive and depend on the model's actual knowledge cutoff; we use existing time-stamped headline datasets straddling the cutoff, multiple probe formats (classification, free-form 'now', event ordering), and report agreement. 4) A positive result on characterization events could reflect memorized event cues rather than a genuine self-model; the unseen-event generalization test (step 6) and the mismatched-base control distinguish these. 5) The time direction may be only approximately linear/multi-directional, so ablation may only partially collapse the shift; we report effect sizes rather than assume clean single-direction control, test multiple early layers, and include a placebo-direction control to guard against activation-readability-without-behavioral-control confounds. 6) Filtering must be strict so the data is genuinely date/event-free; we audit residual leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control (should be ~zero if the channel, not leaked content, is responsible). 7) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, and include a full-finetune comparison. 8) Effects may be model-family and cutoff specific; we test two families and both number and code carriers, and report per-family results.
